48. A player cannot determine before send who receives text, whether it is in fiction, and whether it can change mechanics.

## 30.2 Absolute geometry, presence, orchestration, and dependency launch blockers


### 30.2.1 Absolute local-development, QA-isolation, and deployment blockers

Production publication or phase advancement is blocked if any of the following remains possible:

1. Builder performs ordinary implementation outside Builder Root.
2. QA performs QA work outside QA Root other than approved runtime temporary storage.
3. Either agent can enter, mutate, index, link, mount, or version the other workspace.
4. Workspace authority depends only on agent memory rather than canonical-path checks and sentinels.
5. QA can edit application source or Builder can edit QA expectations or evidence.
6. Ordinary phase QA targets a public, preview, staging, Cloud Run, Firebase Hosting, App Hosting, or custom-domain candidate.
7. A locally served frontend can silently use production Firestore, Authentication, Storage, Functions, WebSocket, or backend services.
8. The Local Stack Manifest is missing, stale, internally inconsistent, or disagrees with actual runtime endpoints.
9. The Emulator Suite UI port is mistaken for a product API and failure causes cloud fallback.
10. The local stack uses a production project ID or production service account during ordinary QA.
11. QA data reset, fixture creation, or cleanup can affect production.
12. Emulator data can be promoted into production ownership, legal, or player records.
13. Certification occurs against hot reload, a dirty tree, a changing bundle, or more than one candidate hash.
14. A source or dependency change during QA execution fails to invalidate the run.
15. A phase lacks the Section 25-required local regression against the same frozen candidate: permanent smoke spine plus impact-selected regression for ordinary phases, and the complete currently applicable cumulative suite only when Phase 6, Phase 7, or an earlier cross-cutting risk trigger requires it.
16. GitHub push, remote pull-request mutation, tag publication, or live deployment can occur without a Product Owner authorization naming the exact candidate and operation.
17. A prior authorization can be used again after source, dependency, configuration, or candidate hash changes.
18. A passing QA report, automated message, timeout, prior phase approval, or deployment credential is treated as authorization.
19. Full regression, destructive chaos, fixture floods, security attacks, or progression sweeps run against the live project as routine practice.
20. Post-deployment smoke is treated as phase certification or creates unapproved live data.
21. A live failure is debugged by repeated production experimentation instead of returning to the local loop.
22. QA evidence, test code, screenshots, traces, videos, or reports are stored in or overwritten by the Builder Root.
23. Application source, build artifacts, secrets, or local commits are stored in the QA Root.
24. The QA target can be changed to a remote origin through an unchecked variable, redirect, stale browser state, proxy, or DNS trick.
25. Required emulator services, reset controls, or local QA capabilities are reachable from a non-loopback interface without explicit temporary approval.
26. Phase 1 or a later phase lacks a recorded Phase 0 certificate and local-environment continuity evidence.
27. Builder Root, QA Root, Runtime Root, Evidence Root, Checkpoint Root, or Pending Archive Root resolves outside `<WORKING_DIRECTORY>`.
28. The Working Directory is online-only, unavailable locally, or redirected in a way that can corrupt active source/runtime/evidence or bypass role ownership.
29. Source, dependencies, emulators, builds, tests, browser profiles, active evidence, credentials, or runtime locks execute from the Archive Directory.
30. An archive operation writes to a path different from the `ARCHIVE_DIRECTORY` recorded for that operation in the Local Stack Manifest, silently selects a fallback path, or changes the configured archive path during a frozen archive operation without updating and revalidating the manifest first.
31. An archive is marked complete without local package hashing, copied-package hashing, and exact reconciliation.
32. Archive-store unavailability blocks unrelated local implementation, testing, remediation, or QA validation instead of producing `ARCHIVE_PENDING`.

### 30.2.2 Absolute geometry, presence, orchestration, and dependency production launch blockers

Production launch is blocked if any of the following remains possible:

1. A mechanical area origin is derived from arbitrary screen pixels or unrestricted client floating-point coordinates.
2. A pointer movement within one canonical anchor changes the target set.
3. Hidden information changes area snapping, orientation availability, propagation preview, timing, labels, or sound.
4. An effect that spreads around corners is resolved solely by direct rays.
5. An ordinary direct effect bends through cover because the engine applies generic flood fill.
6. A sphere, cone, cube, wall, or other bounded solid is implemented as an unlimited vertical extrusion.
7. Elevation, floors, ceilings, shafts, or vertical cover are ignored when they are mechanically relevant.
8. Client and server disagree on anchor, normalized orientation, three-dimensional volume, propagation plan, or affected targets.
9. A diagonal path, smoothed path, forced move, animation, mount, grapple, or large footprint can cross a blocked vertex or clearance channel.
10. AI or player narrative text can trigger sound, animation, camera, particles, notifications, or mechanics.
11. A decisive sound plays without the corresponding authorized visual or accessible event milestone.
12. Reconnect, retry, second tab, or narrative restart duplicates a cue.
13. Closing the browser, timing out, or selecting Leave Session removes a character from active Initiative or relocates them to safety.
14. An absent combat character becomes immune, untargetable, stabilized, or protected from ordinary rules without a valid effect.
15. A build context contains unmanifested transcripts, duplicated blueprint bodies, superseded implementation instructions, or contaminated trailing text.
16. An agent continues past a human-review gate without a durable authenticated approval for the exact frozen candidate hash.
17. Silence, timeout, tool completion, an AI statement, or an approval for another candidate is treated as human approval.
18. QA can change package manifests or lockfiles, or Builder can introduce an unrecorded/high-risk dependency that bypasses the dependency governance in Section 1.10.9.
19. `@pixi/react`, another unapproved Pixi wrapper, remote package script, or second render-state authority is present in the Alpha 3 production graph.
20. The frozen candidate's dependency graph differs from its tested software bill of materials.
21. Any required regression fails.

## 30.3 Absolute code-completeness, quality-first, and evidence-integrity blockers

Phase advancement, Public Milestone authorization, Gold Master authorization, and remote publication are blocked if any of the following remains possible:

1. Builder declares completion before every in-scope Requirement Ledger entry is passed or approved not applicable.
2. Current-phase behavior relies on a TODO, FIXME, stub, hardcoded success, empty handler, fake UI control, incomplete branch, unimplemented interface, disabled validation, inappropriate mock, or certification-only bypass.
3. A required end-to-end path lacks authorization, persistence, event, projection, player feedback, error, retry, reconnect, recovery, security, or regression behavior that is in scope.
4. The Code Completeness Scan is missing, stale, excludes affected files, or has unresolved blocking findings.
5. A generated file is truncated, syntactically closed but semantically incomplete, or contains unreviewed repeated or omitted branches caused by context or output limits.
6. Builder shortens scope, omits required cases, weakens assertions, skips browsers, or defers in-scope behavior because of token, context, time, or tool pressure.
7. The candidate bypasses `BUILDER_VERIFYING` or the implementing agent is the only role that evaluated readiness.
8. A pass status is created from agent prose, Markdown, a checklist, a matrix table, a screenshot caption, an expected-output file, or a manually authored result rather than actual execution evidence.
9. A required test was not discovered, selected, executed, or asserted but is reported passed.
10. A test process catches failures, times out, crashes, terminates early, or lacks required dependencies while returning or being summarized as success.
11. A matrix lacks a pre-execution manifest or post-execution exact reconciliation of required case IDs.
12. Required cases are missing, duplicated, substituted, skipped, blocked, or flaky while the summary says the full matrix passed.
13. Evidence was copied from another candidate, environment, baseline, browser, or earlier run.
14. Source, test, schema, dependency, configuration, baseline, or environment changed after execution without invalidating affected evidence.
15. Completed raw result evidence can be edited in place without invalidating its hash or preserving the original attempt.
16. Builder manually authors or alters authoritative pass records, assertion totals, run identifiers, timestamps, browser versions, exit codes, hashes, or result JSON.
17. A report exists but the referenced raw results, process output, traces, logs, state assertions, or hashes do not exist or do not reconcile.
18. Zero-test discovery or zero meaningful assertions can produce a passing suite.
19. Re-running a flaky test until green hides earlier failures or excludes them from the evidence package.
20. A blocked, not executed, environment-failed, or uncertain result defaults to pass.
21. QA finds a defect that Builder verification claimed to cover and Builder neither classifies the escape nor improves permanent regression coverage.
22. A verification-integrity failure occurs and the candidate’s entire Builder Verification Package is not invalidated and rerun from a clean state.
23. The phase report lacks the Code and Evidence Completeness Declaration or its referenced evidence fails validation.

The governing rule is absolute: reports may describe executed success; they may never manufacture it.


## 30.4 Absolute holistic product, visual, provider, and originality blockers

The product cannot launch when any of the following is true:

- The title or logo lacks documented clearance or resembles protected trade dress.
- The SRD attribution is missing, misleading, or suggests endorsement.
- An unregistered provider, model, SDK, font, icon, sound, image source, analytics service, or monitoring service is used.
- Provider terms, region, tier, age, data-handling, safety, or branding review is stale or incomplete.
- External player login offers anything other than the approved Google-only flow after cutover.
- The Google sign-in control violates current branding guidance or requests unnecessary scopes.
- A public password field or development-login route remains available.
- Quick-start templates are incomplete, named after protected characters, mechanically invalid, shared as one canonical character, or missing visual assets.
- Normal game play is primarily a text thread beside a blank, monochrome, or diagnostic grid.
- A tactical encounter starts without validated image-backed map art and readable tokens, except during a clearly identified emergency degraded mode.
- Avatars, portraits, and tokens drift across identity or become indistinguishable.
- Secret map art or entity assets are delivered before authorization or remain accessible to another account after logout.
- Fog is the only control protecting hidden content.
- Looping graphics obscure play, ignore reduced motion, continue wastefully in hidden tabs, or cause frame-budget failure without graceful downgrade.
- Full-effects visual requirements are certified using only static fallback evidence.
- A brand, persistent portrait, map, scene, sound, or logo asset lacks provenance and rights review.
- Generated output contains protected content, real-person likeness, watermark, embedded logo, signature, or unreviewed spoiler.
- AI, identity, or asset-provider certification relies only on mocks.
- The landing, login, dashboard, character, and game screens appear to be unrelated products.
- Required **Section 25.4 / publication / Phase 7 release evidence or approvals** for the exact candidate are missing: Product Owner visual/experience approval at the named gates; applicable external legal/brand/provider clearance for the intended publication; required security/privacy/accessibility certification evidence; or the Phase 5 Product Owner complete-game-feel review (including whether the experience is sufficiently fun/coherent to continue). This line creates no additional unnamed human gate.

# APPENDIX A — PRODUCT SCOPE, LOCKED DECISIONS, AND PRODUCT-OWNER ACCEPTANCE

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## A.SCOPE — PRODUCT NON-GOALS FOR ALPHA 3

Alpha 3 does not require:

- Anonymous public matchmaking.
- A dedicated child/minor-targeted product mode. Eligibility for ordinary players follows the active provider and applicable law rather than a permanent Alpha 3 under-18 exclusion.
- User-created public marketplaces.
- Real-money trading.
- Blockchain assets.
- Mod execution.
- unrestricted scripting.
- Full mobile tactical play.
- video generation.
- music generation.
- celebrity voices.
- franchise crossover content.
- unmoderated public campaign discovery.
- AI control over player characters.
- Unbounded AI authority over mechanics or direct AI state mutation.
- photorealistic depictions of real people.

These exclusions protect focus, safety, cost, and completion.

---

## A.LOCKED — LOCKED ALPHA 3 PRODUCT DECISION REGISTER

The Product Owner has answered all decisions below. They are locked for Alpha 3. An implementation agent may not restore an earlier recommended default, leave the choice configurable, or move the requirement later than the phase already assigned by Section 25 without a new Product Owner-approved decision record. **Section 25's existing deferral of a locked future-state capability is already authorized and is not itself a forbidden deferral.**

## A.LOCKED.1 Primary play mode

**Locked:** Two to six human players are primary. Solo is supported secondarily. Multiplayer behavior drives certification **once the roadmap brings multiplayer behavior into scope**; earlier phase certificates prove only the narrower Section 25 journey and never claim final representative-experience certification.

## A.LOCKED.2 Communication

**Locked:** Built-in accessible text chat. External Discord or equivalent voice is assumed when groups want voice, but it is not integrated or required. No private player-to-player messaging in Alpha 3.


### A.LOCKED.2.1 Communication Dock and action input

**Locked:** Chronicle, Party Chat, and Rules Desk are top-level peer destinations. Party Chat is never nested inside Rules Desk. Mechanical actions use a separate Action Composer with Intent Intercept. Ordinary Party Chat is not automatically given to the AI Director. Players may explicitly address the Director through a nonmechanical `@DM` or Address the DM workflow, which can offer an Action Composer draft but cannot act.

## A.LOCKED.3 Game Director identity, personality, and speech

**Locked:** Campaign creation requires selecting one of two single-name Game Directors—**Veyra** (female) or **Garrick** (male)—and then selecting one concrete approved campaign personality. That identity/personality pair persists for the campaign and ordinary users cannot change it after creation. The selected personality deterministically selects the corresponding Veyra/Garrick avatar variant; avatar is not a third player choice. Only a server-authorized administrator may override identity or personality, and every override is audited.

Game Director and approved NPC narration remain canonically stored and displayed as text, and screen readers remain supported independently. Alpha 3 includes Phase 4 **player-optional text-to-speech and speech-to-text**. TTS follows the selected campaign Director's voice family and can only speak already approved visible text. STT produces an editable unsent draft in the currently selected composer and never submits or confirms anything automatically. A player may use either capability, both, or neither.

## A.LOCKED.4 Human facilitation

**Locked:** No human facilitator is required. The AI runs the table. A human campaign owner controls ordinary campaign administration and safety but cannot change the locked Game Director identity/personality after campaign creation and never controls another player's character or roll.

### A.LOCKED.4.1 Bootstrap administrator and Admin interface

**Locked:** Hallucinated Dungeons has a Phase 4 account-based Admin interface. The exact server-verified Google account `nick.donner@gmail.com` is the permanent bootstrap administrator and cannot be demoted through ordinary product administration. Client-provided email values never grant admin authority. Administrator is an additional capability, not a replacement player account type: the same account may play normally and receives elevated authority only on explicitly authorized Admin operations. Admin operations are server-authorized and audited, and administrator status never grants silent gameplay mutation, hidden-player information, or player impersonation.

## A.LOCKED.5 Starter adventure

**Locked:** Ship one original curated three-to-five-session starter campaign. It is the primary onboarding path and a fixed validation fixture.

## A.LOCKED.6 Map generation and persistence

**Locked:** Hybrid map pipeline using reviewed mechanical layouts and original visual treatment. Any admitted live map and all tactical state resume exactly after players leave and return. Active map regeneration is prohibited.

## A.LOCKED.7 Dice

**Locked:** Server-only authoritative dice. No physical or manually entered results. The system determines the expression. Present players click a context-specific Roll button. Animation is quick, optional in intensity, and never the randomness source. Rules-authorized rerolls, replacements, and choose-between-results features use typed Decision Windows linked to the original roll; no generic outcome-shopping reroll exists.

## A.LOCKED.8 Character source and portability

**Locked:** Characters are created only inside Hallucinated Dungeons. No character import, playable export, or re-import in Alpha 3.

### A.LOCKED.8.1 Character wizard order and SRD vocabulary

**Locked:** Character creation uses the approved SRD 5.2.1 names and familiar terms—Class, Background, Species, Hit Points (HP), Armor Class (AC), Speed, and the other applicable SRD mechanics. Hallucinated Dungeons may add novice-friendly explanations but does not rename those rules concepts. The custom wizard defines mechanics first and places **Identity & Final Review last**; quick-start likewise chooses/reviews the mechanical template before the player supplies the character's identity and creates the character.

## A.LOCKED.9 Character death

**Locked:** Follow the rules and committed results. Lawful rescue opportunities may occur before death. A committed death receives memorable character-specific memorial narration and remains a dead, potentially revivable state until a legal revival succeeds, revival becomes impossible, or the account owner permanently retires the character.

## A.LOCKED.10 Absent characters

**Locked:** No player receives another player's unrestricted character interface or ownership. Rules-valid compulsion may constrain the owner's legal options or deterministically execute mandatory behavior without transferring control. Voluntary leave, logout, timeout, or expired disconnect grace triggers bounded deterministic Departure Handling. **During active Initiative, the character remains in its canonical square under the Dodge-or-end-turn absence lock and cannot be moved, removed, or narrated out because of absence.** Narrated exit occurs only after a legal non-Initiative departure event commits. Return requires legal placement followed by narrated entry.

## A.LOCKED.11 Campaign duration

**Locked:** Generate a structured campaign skeleton without imposing a terminal endpoint. Campaigns may continue, branch, and create new chapters after a planned climax.

## A.LOCKED.12 Undo and retcon

**Locked:** No gameplay undo, retcon, rewind, reload exploit, or unauthorized outcome-shopping reroll. Valid committed events stand. Rules-authorized rerolls, replacements, saving throws, and revival attempts are forward-moving canonical procedures. Audited correction events exist only for verified defects, corruption, duplicates, or unauthorized state.

## A.LOCKED.13 Party disagreement

**Locked:** Use summarized options, discussion, and the campaign's selected majority, unanimous, or caller policy. Group process never controls another character or supplies consent for its owner.

## A.LOCKED.14 Tone and humor

**Locked:** Adventurous fantasy with danger, atmosphere, hope, and room for serious moments. The Director is tuned toward roughly thirty percent humor across representative humor-eligible play, with a normal-play minimum target of twenty percent in QA/session evaluation. This is a tone-quality floor for representative samples, not a runtime joke quota or per-window command. Safety, legal/security, consent, and deliberately serious exempt responses are outside that denominator rather than forced to joke.

## A.LOCKED.15 Product description

**Locked:** “An original 5e-compatible AI fantasy tabletop built using SRD 5.2.1 under CC BY 4.0.” Do not imply official endorsement or full commercial-book coverage.

## A.LOCKED.16 Alpha business model

**Locked:** Persistent/AI-backed Alpha gameplay is private, invitation-only, and unpaid; Section 1.11.14 Public Showcases are the only public-view exception. No checkout, subscription, premium mechanics, or paid Director treatment.

## A.LOCKED.17 Campaign export

**Locked:** No campaign, map, chronicle, or playable-character export in Alpha 3. Legally required privacy-data access remains separate and non-importable.

## A.LOCKED.18 Devices and browsers

**Locked:** Current desktop Chrome and Edge are primary; current Firefox and Safari are required secondary; certified tablets are fully playable; phones are companion-only; no installation is required. Final Safari/tablet certification follows the evidence-timing rule in Section 1.5.18 and does not block ordinary earlier-phase work on a host OS that cannot run those browsers natively.

## A.LOCKED.19 Tactical grid

**Locked:** One native five-foot square grid for exact tactical play. Gridless presentation is allowed only when position is not mechanically relevant.

## A.LOCKED.20 Drop-in combat

**Locked default:** Next Round Entry at a validated access point, with observer-until-entry behavior. Immediate entry is permitted only through an explicit valid pre-commit Director ruling and cannot grant a duplicate turn or unsafe forced placement.

## A.LOCKED.21 Rules transparency

**Locked default:** Players see roll breakdowns, applicable rule identifiers, and Director adjustment summaries without receiving hidden target numbers or secret information prematurely.

## A.LOCKED.22 Director discretion

**Locked default:** Moderate bounded discretion. The Director may make lawful fun-first rulings and comparable improvised actions but cannot alter revealed dice, ownership, safety, visibility, resource integrity, or committed events.

## A.LOCKED.23 PvP

**Locked default:** Explicit affected-player consent is required for hostile mechanical actions between player characters. Social rolls never compel another player character's internal state.

## A.LOCKED.24 Rules content

**Locked:** Reviewed SRD 5.2.1 content plus clearly original reviewed campaign content. No unlicensed commercial-book options.

## A.LOCKED.25 Public access

**Locked:** Invitation-only private campaigns. No anonymous matchmaking or public campaign directory in Alpha 3.


## A.LOCKED.26 Adult eligibility experience

**Locked:** Enforce an eighteen-or-older restriction only while the selected production provider or applicable law requires it. When active, use the least intrusive compliant authenticated mechanism and do not collect exact birth dates, identity documents, biometrics, or payment proxies without a separate requirement. When provider/legal review permits broader access, the gate may be disabled without architectural change.

## A.LOCKED.27 Palette direction and freedom

**Locked:** Obsidian Chronicle with an obsidian-blue bias remains the initial design direction, but no hue is prohibited. Palette decisions are governed by readability, accessibility, semantic consistency, tactical clarity, and human aesthetic review.

## A.LOCKED.28 Product voice and humor

**Locked:** The product is clear, atmospheric, and witty throughout eligible UX copy. The Director is calibrated to a normal-play minimum target of twenty percent humor signal across representative humor-eligible QA/session samples, defaults near thirty percent, and adapts upward by persona without turning the target into a runtime punchline quota.

## A.LOCKED.29 Opening identity sequence

**Locked:** The hosted public landing page includes a smooth, skippable, nonblocking, reduced-motion-safe opening animation that forms and resolves into **Hallucinated Dungeons**, then blends into the usable landing page. It uses no required video and no replay during active-session resume or ordinary navigation; optional Director speech is a separate player setting, not part of the blocking intro.

## A.LOCKED.30 Advancement mode

**Locked:** Experience Points are the sole advancement trigger. Milestone advancement is excluded from Alpha 3.

## A.LOCKED.31 Class progression

**Locked:** Characters advance only in the class selected at creation through level 20. Multiclassing is excluded from Alpha 3.

## A.LOCKED.32 Progression QA harness

**Locked:** The Local Arena includes a capability-authorized, fixture-scoped Progression QA Harness that exercises the same canonical XP and level-up services used by hosted play. The harness capability is not exposed in Milestone or Launch Production. The exact `QA ` name prefix is labeling only and grants no authority.

## A.LOCKED.33 Development and QA identity

**Locked:** Internal development and automated QA may use server-minted temporary identities and machine-only test sessions without a Google account. No Hallucinated Dungeons password system is introduced. Test authority is short-lived, allowlisted, audited, revocable, and restricted to disposable fixtures.

## A.LOCKED.34 External Alpha identity

**Locked:** Before external Alpha player access, Google Sign-In becomes the only player-facing identity provider. Machine-only fixture QA may remain without a Google account, but public development login is disabled and cannot serve ordinary players.


## A.LOCKED.35 Visual product standard

The normal game must be a graphically rich visual tabletop, not a text thread beside a black-and-white grid. Image-backed maps or illustrated scenes, avatars, tokens, fog, lighting, effects, and appropriate motion are required.

## A.LOCKED.36 Logo and brand

Alpha 3 uses one original, cleared Hallucinated Dungeons logo family across landing, login, dashboard, table, legal, and error surfaces.

## A.LOCKED.37 Quick-start characters

Alpha 3 includes unnamed, original, rules-valid quick-start templates for every supported class. Selection creates a new account-owned character. A name is required before table entry.

## A.LOCKED.38 Secret visual assets

Fog never substitutes for asset authorization. Unrevealed map art, rooms, doors, entities, and portraits are not delivered to unauthorized clients.

## A.LOCKED.39 Ambient motion

Appropriate scenes use restrained looped and event-bound motion, with complete reduced-motion and performance fallbacks. Motion serves atmosphere and clarity rather than spectacle for its own sake.

## A.LOCKED.40 Provider compliance

Every external provider is registered and reviewed against current official terms, regional restrictions, age limits, data use, safety, attribution, branding, and service-tier requirements before release.

## A.LOCKED.41 Intellectual-property boundary

No unlicensed third-party intellectual property is used. SRD 5.2.1 material is used only under its approved CC BY 4.0 attribution; all other expression and brand assets are original or separately licensed.

## A.LOCKED.42 Actual-provider certification

Mocks may support development, but in-scope AI, identity, and asset services receive actual approved-path testing before phase or launch certification.

## A.DECISIONS — PRODUCT OWNER DECISION ACCEPTANCE MATRIX

This appendix converts the locked decisions into black-box evidence. Every scenario runs against the same frozen local candidate served by the Local Arena used for phase certification. A screenshot alone is insufficient; evidence includes account identities, commands, events, projections, UI recordings, accessibility output, model records where relevant, and final canonical state.

## A.DECISIONS.1 Multiplayer-primary certification

Run one solo session, one two-player session, one four-player session, and one six-player session through login, seating, exploration, combat, chat, leave, return, and session suspension. Confirm that adding players does not expose hidden state, duplicate turns, change ownership, or force a human facilitator. At least half of moderated Alpha usability hours must involve three or more simultaneous human or independently simulated players.

## A.DECISIONS.2 Text communication and optional speech input/output certification

Verify Party Chat (including the explicit Table Talk and Speak as Character modes) and the private Director Address workflow are visually distinct, keyboard accessible, moderated, escaped, persisted, and audience filtered. Verify there is no voice-conference dependency, stored player voice message, spatial voice, or Discord login, and no rule information is available only through audio or external communication. A player using neither text-to-speech nor speech-to-text must complete the starter campaign.

For **Veyra** and **Garrick**, enable text-to-speech and verify playback uses an approved voice compatible with that identity, matches the approved visible text, obeys mute/rate/volume/autoplay settings, leaks no hidden information, never delays mechanics, and falls back to text without blocking play.

Enable speech-to-text separately on every relevant composer. Verify microphone permission is requested only after explicit player action; transcription appears as an editable unsent draft in the currently selected composer; denied permission leaves typing usable; and dictation never auto-sends, changes composer type, confirms an Intent Intercept, chooses a Reaction, rolls dice, or mutates state.

### A.DECISIONS.2.1 Communication Dock and Action Composer certification

Verify Chronicle, Party Chat, and Rules Desk are peer destinations and the Action Composer is separate. Submit identical text through Party Chat, Speak as Character, Rules Desk, Director Address, and Action Composer. Confirm human chat remains nonmechanical, in-character speech creates only the approved communication fact, Rules Desk remains explanatory, Director Address remains nonmechanical, and only the confirmed Action Composer path can create a command.

Run the same matrix during another player's turn, an active Reaction, a roll prompt, narrative streaming, disconnect, reconnect, tablet layout, keyboard navigation, screen reader use, 200% zoom, and shared-computer logout. Verify no cross-surface draft leakage, no AI use of ordinary Party Chat, and no focus theft from urgent prompts.

## A.DECISIONS.3 Persistent Director identity and personality

Create campaigns with every combination of **Veyra / Garrick** and each approved personality through the real campaign-creation page. Verify the player must explicitly select a Director and then explicitly select/confirm a personality; a visually recommended Friendly Adventurer option cannot silently become the campaign choice. Verify each combination resolves to the correct personality-specific avatar, the Director remains recognizable across avatar variants, and the selected identity/personality/avatar combination survives refresh, logout/login, reconnect, server-worker replacement, model fallback, campaign resume, and chapter transition. Verify personality changes tone/presentation only and cannot change deterministic rules, difficulty, resource cost, hidden-information access, target legality, or the ruling envelope. Verify ordinary campaign owners and players cannot alter it after campaign creation.

Beginning in Phase 4, use the Admin interface to override identity, personality, and both together. Verify the derived avatar changes with the new configuration at the safe boundary, authorization, reason capture, before/after values, audit history, persistence after reload, and no rewrite of earlier Chronicle attribution. Attempt the same override as an ordinary player, campaign owner, spoofed-email client, and support role without the required permission; all must fail. Then use the bootstrap-administrator account as an ordinary player and verify its character, seat, perception, rolls, commands, and hidden-information access are identical to an equivalent non-admin player except when an explicit Admin operation is invoked.

Measure the humor signal over representative humor-eligible session samples or an equivalent QA corpus. The minimum target is twenty percent and the default begins near thirty percent; no runtime counter forces short-term quota repair, and serious excluded categories are not forced to joke. Verify Sassy remains playful rather than insulting and Encouraging does not become patronizing.

## A.DECISIONS.4 AI-only table operation

Create and run a campaign without a human facilitator role. Verify the AI opens scenes, manages turns, requests rolls, adjudicates, narrates, and handles recaps. Separately verify the human campaign owner can invite, pause, remove, report, and configure safety but cannot issue another character's command, alter a roll, view unauthorized secrets, or bypass policy.

## A.DECISIONS.5 Starter campaign fixture

During Phase 5, QA completes the curated starter campaign using novice-behavior, experienced-behavior, and mixed-group test profiles; Product Owner-scheduled human cohorts supplement this at the explicit experience/hardening gates rather than becoming a hidden prerequisite for earlier phases. Verify three-to-five-session pacing under expected session lengths, at least one social resolution, one tactical encounter, one spell area, one environmental improvisation, one failure that moves forward, one player absence and return, and a satisfying climax. Later candidates that touch campaign systems use the same versioned start state and rerun the impacted campaign checkpoints under Section 25; the complete multi-session campaign is rerun in Phases 6 and 7 or earlier only when the change materially affects campaign-wide continuity or pacing.

## A.DECISIONS.6 Exact map resume

Suspend a campaign after each of the following: moving a token, opening a door, revealing fog, damaging an object, creating a persistent zone, summoning a creature, starting a new round, presenting a reaction, streaming narration, and disconnecting every client. Clear browser caches and replace the realtime worker. Resume from another supported browser. Compare map bundle hashes, event sequence, token anchors, objects, fog, initiative, resources, and zones byte-for-byte or through approved canonical equivalence. No active map may be regenerated.

## A.DECISIONS.7 Player-triggered dice

For attacks, saves, checks, initiative where player activation is appropriate, death saves, Advantage, Disadvantage, and multiple-die damage, verify the interface provides the correct context-specific button and no die picker. Attempt manual entry, DOM modification, repeat activation, stale activation, two-device activation, reconnect, and replay. Confirm one server result. Then test an approved rules-authorized reroll and a choose-between-results feature: preserve the original roll, open one typed Decision Window, spend the resource once, and identify the operative result. Reject a generic reroll request with no legal feature. Measure default presentation and fail routine animations exceeding the approved ceiling. Verify chat remains usable before activation.

## A.DECISIONS.8 In-product characters only

Search routes, settings, APIs, upload handlers, and UI for character import or portable gameplay export. Attempt files, pasted JSON, third-party URLs, and copied sheets. Reject without creating canonical character state. Create and level a character entirely in the site and verify derived values against the SRD manifest.

### A.DECISIONS.8.1 Identity-last SRD character-wizard certification

Start a custom character and verify the wizard presents the actual approved **Class**, **Background**, and **Species** names before collecting personal identity. Continue through Ability Scores/Proficiencies, Equipment, and applicable Class Feature/Spell choices. Confirm that **Identity & Final Review is the last wizard step**, and that name, pronouns, appearance, portrait/visual treatment, and optional concept are not required earlier. On the final step, verify the page uses familiar labels including **Hit Points (HP), Armor Class (AC), Speed, Initiative, and Proficiency Bonus** and contains no replacement-stat vocabulary such as Vitality, Guard, Stride, Resolve, Focus, or Path-as-Class. Repeat with a quick-start template: select and review the mechanical template first, then provide identity at the final step.

## A.DECISIONS.9 Death memorial experience

Execute character death through ordinary damage, failed death saves, and an effect that does not permit death saves where supported. Verify fixed results, no unauthorized post-death rescue, no undo, one Character Death Event, and one linked Character Memorial Event. Test each memorial tone profile. Confirm narration matches events, preserves dignity, does not invent achievements, and does not falsely declare revival impossible. Attempt an invalid revival, a valid revival accepted by the owner, a valid revival refused by the owner, and permanent retirement. Confirm the death remains in campaign history and only the account owner can retire the character.

## A.DECISIONS.10 Narrated departure and return

Test voluntary Step Away, Leave Session, logout, closed tab, laptop sleep, network loss within grace, network loss past grace, timeout during own turn, disconnect after roll activation, and campaign-owner removal both outside and during active Initiative. **During Initiative, confirm the character never moves/removes due to absence, remains targetable in the same canonical square, uses only the locked Dodge-or-end-turn policy, and receives no departure narration until Initiative ends.** Outside Initiative, confirm bounded Departure Handling, no other-player command acceptance, committed exit before narration, absent command lockout, legal return placement, personal recap, and committed arrival before narration.

## A.DECISIONS.11 Open-ended continuation

Finish the starter campaign climax and continue play. Verify chapter renewal preserves history, offers grounded new directions, accepts a player-created goal, builds only validated next content, and does not mark the campaign permanently complete. Run a long-memory test with archived chapters and confirm retrieval does not reveal secrets or exceed context budgets.

## A.DECISIONS.12 No undo

Attempt undo before and after a roll, after hidden information, after another player's action, after death, after loot allocation, and through campaign-owner/admin interfaces. No gameplay rewind exists. Verify that an approved reroll feature and a legal revival attempt remain available because they advance the canonical timeline rather than rewriting it. Inject a verified duplicate-event defect in staging and confirm the narrow correction process repairs canonical state without granting a new decision or erasing audit history.

## A.DECISIONS.13 Party disagreement

Present three conflicting party plans under no time pressure and under immediate danger. Test majority, unanimous, and caller policies. Confirm the Director summarizes accurately, avoids favoring message order, allows split action where fiction permits, and never binds another character's action, belief, PvP consent, or personal item.

## A.DECISIONS.14 Humor target

Run at least three sessions with humor set to the Alpha default. Classify ordinary Director responses against the approved humor rubric and verify an approximate thirty-percent rolling target without joke spam. Include serious injury, character death, safety intervention, rules correction, and connection failure; confirm humor suppression unless explicitly appropriate. Collect player ratings on group laughter, timing, repetition, and tonal harm.

## A.DECISIONS.15 Compatibility and attribution

Inspect landing, legal, campaign creation, help, and marketing copy. Confirm the approved 5e-compatible SRD language, complete CC BY attribution, and absence of official-endorsement claims, protected logos, or promises of full commercial-book content.

## A.DECISIONS.16 Closed unpaid Alpha

Search the hosted product and source configuration for checkout, payment providers, subscriptions, premium credits, paid queues, donations that unlock service, or monetized mechanics. Verify invite-only capacity and equal mechanical treatment across accounts.

## A.DECISIONS.17 No gameplay export

Attempt character, campaign, map, chronicle, and world export through UI and APIs. No portable format exists. Execute a privacy-data access request and verify its disclosures meet policy while remaining clearly labeled non-playable and rejected by every import endpoint because no import endpoint exists.

## A.DECISIONS.18 Browser and device matrix

During Phase 6/7 support certification, run the complete core loop on current desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and **real Safari** according to Section 1.5.18's browser-evidence timing rule. Run the certified tablet loop including map movement and spell targeting on appropriate real hardware or an approved device service. On phones, verify companion features and clear prevention of unsupported tactical control. Earlier local phases may use engine-level coverage where native hardware is unavailable but may not mislabel that evidence as Safari/tablet certification. Install nothing, grant no extension permission, and verify unsupported WebGL states produce a truthful fallback or blocker.


## A.DECISIONS.19 Adult affirmation certification

Create, decline, accept, revoke, corrupt, and version the adult-eligibility record. When the active provider requires adult eligibility, verify one valid account-level acceptance survives logout, supported browser changes, invitations, refresh, and reconnect without repeat prompting; verify no restricted provider request occurs before acceptance and no exact birth date, identity document, biometric evidence, or payment proxy is collected without separate authority. When the provider does not require the gate, verify the application does not collect an adult affirmation unnecessarily.

## A.DECISIONS.20 Palette and visual-coherence certification

Capture every implemented route and important component state. Conduct automated contrast/color-independent-meaning checks and **Builder/QA player-use visual review** for visual cohesion, tactical readability, fatigue, semantic consistency, and whether the obsidian-blue direction still feels intentional. Product Owner visual review joins only when the candidate is at an explicit Section 25 visual/publication/release gate. No hue fails merely because it is purple, pink, blue, or otherwise prominent; aesthetic excess is filed as an ordinary visual defect.

## A.DECISIONS.21 Product-voice certification

Review all implemented UX strings and a representative Director-response corpus. Verify clarity precedes humor, serious classifications suppress wit, repeated errors do not become joke loops, and ordinary eligible copy feels personable without becoming sarcastic or performative. Collect player ratings for usefulness, warmth, group-laughter support, repetition, embarrassment, and comedian fatigue.

## A.DECISIONS.22 Opening-sequence certification

Run clean first visit, repeat visit, skip, reduced motion, high contrast, forced colors, low graphics, slow network, animation failure, blocked sound, invitation continuation, authenticated deep link, reconnect, and active-session resume on the supported browser and tablet matrix. Verify the full sequence resolves into **Hallucinated Dungeons**, never exceeds four seconds, never blocks the underlying page, and never replaces core loading or recovery feedback. Optional Director speech is tested separately and cannot become a landing-page gate.

## A.DECISIONS.23 Final product-owner lock gate

Before controlled Alpha launch, the Product Owner or explicitly delegated human release reviewer records one approval row for every locked decision with linked evidence. Any unresolved contradiction between code, prompts, context packs, tests, or this register blocks launch. “Implemented differently by the agent” is not an acceptable disposition.

This blueprint was aligned against official materials reviewed through August 11, 2026. Static review does not replace release-time verification. The controlling set includes:

A provider or model not selected for the candidate does not create an implementation obligation merely because it appeared in an earlier research note. The current versions of all applicable official materials supersede this appendix.

# APPENDIX C — BUILDER EXECUTION, CONTEXT, LOCAL ARENA, TESTING, AND EVIDENCE INTEGRITY

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## C.EXEC — BUILDER GREENFIELD EXECUTION DIRECTIVE

Treat V1 as the sole implementation and certification authority.

Begin from an empty production source tree. The repository may contain V1, approved provider documentation, approved licensed rules data, and the minimal Phase 0 bootstrap instructions. It must not contain application source, tests, schemas, fixtures, assets, database exports, reports, or evidence from another implementation.

Execute these directives:

1. Create the greenfield repository structure during Phase 0 using recorded baseline runtime, package-manager, package-boundary, local-stack, and lightweight evidence choices; do not create a separate approval ceremony for ordinary bootstrap decisions.
2. Implement phases strictly in integer order from Phase 0 through Phase 7.
3. Do not create decimal, inserted, emergency, or unofficial phases.
4. Do not load superseded blueprints, conversation transcripts, generated summaries, or unmanifested reference bundles into implementation context.
5. Use the Context Diet and Shared Invariant Kernel. Give each subagent only the phase requirements, owned contracts, relevant schemas, required tests, and prohibited domains needed for its task.
6. Author every production file under V1 and record its requirement and phase ownership.
7. Implement one native five-foot square tactical model. Do not create a topology selector, compatibility converter, alternate coordinate path, or generic runtime topology switch.
8. Treat gridless scenes only as presentation modes for situations where exact position has no mechanical consequence.
9. Use Vanilla PixiJS directly for the tactical renderer. Do not install an unapproved rendering wrapper or create a second visual-state authority.
10. Render canonical mechanical truth only from server-produced projections. Local state may preview intent and animate committed events but may never declare a mutation complete.
11. Keep the browser, AI models, and process memory non-authoritative.
12. Build the local client, server, WebSocket service, Firebase emulators, seed tooling, and evidence collector as the Local Arena.
13. Resolve Builder Root as `<WORKING_DIRECTORY>/Builder` and QA Root as `<WORKING_DIRECTORY>/QA`; record the resolved absolute Working Directory in the Local Stack Manifest. Record `ARCHIVE_DIRECTORY` only when one is configured.
14. Allow Builder and QA to read both roots. Enforce separate write ownership.
15. Keep all ordinary development, destructive testing, matrix execution, chaos testing, and player validation local.
16. Fail closed when a normal local path attempts to reach a public project, live player database, public Authentication tenant, public Storage bucket, hosted server, or production credential.
17. Do not push or deploy until the Product Owner authorizes the exact frozen candidate, target environment, milestone mode, refs, and capabilities. Only the Phase 7 Gold Master may deploy to Launch Production.
18. Implement complete in-scope code. Do not use TODOs, stubs, hardcoded success, fake UI, unresolved mocks, swallowed errors, disabled validation, or “coming later” behavior for a requirement owned by the current phase.
19. Future-phase behavior may be absent. It may not be represented by a deceptive placeholder.
20. Maintain one lean Phase Requirement Ledger and keep it synchronized with actual implementation/evidence; do not create ceremonial per-task ledgers unless useful.
21. Builder must implement, diagnose, fix, rerun focused/integration tests, perform the actual-page self-play journey, run the permanent smoke spine plus impact-based regression, and continue without routine Product Owner prompting. Deep independent challenge and full cumulative regression are required in Phases 6 and 7 or when risk triggers them earlier.
22. Do not stop for ordinary bugs, test failures, refactoring choices, local service restarts, or fixture design.
22a. Do not present an implementation plan, task plan, file-change plan, or proposed approach and wait for Product Owner approval before ordinary authorized local work. Internal plans are executed immediately.
22b. A forced session continuation resumes from the latest durable checkpoint and does not reopen planning or request renewed authorization.
23. When context pressure approaches, save a durable checkpoint, ledger, changed-file manifest, test state, open defects, and exact next actions; continue in a fresh scoped context.
24. Never reduce scope or manufacture completion because a context or execution window is ending.
25. A test passes only when the real test ran, required assertions executed, the candidate produced the expected result, and machine-verifiable evidence binds the result to that candidate and environment.
26. Markdown summaries describe evidence. They never create success.
27. Treat fabricated, copied, edited, zero-work, stale, or nonexecuted pass evidence as a Critical Process Integrity Defect.
28. Create and reconcile Matrix Manifests only for the explicit conformance/security/browser/progression matrices that require them; ordinary focused tests do not need matrix paperwork.
29. Freeze a candidate before QA player validation.
30. QA tests the same local candidate as a player and writes authoritative findings under QA Root.
31. Builder consumes the complete findings file, reproduces every open defect, adds regression coverage where appropriate, fixes the implementation, reruns Builder verification, and returns a new frozen candidate.
32. Builder does not alter or close QA findings. QA closes them only after player-facing retest.
33. Use the deterministic rules engine for rolls, movement, resources, damage, healing, conditions, equipment, reactions, durations, XP, level advancement, and canonical mutation.
34. Use XP-only single-class advancement through level 20. Do not implement milestone advancement or multiclassing.
35. Use server-issued Timing Authority for every encounter mutation, including valid out-of-turn opportunities.
36. Keep Party Chat, Chronicle, Rules Desk, Director Address, and Action Composer separate in UI, storage, authorization, and AI routing.
37. Omit hidden records entirely from player-facing AI payloads and clients.
38. Implement image-backed maps, avatars, tokens, fog, lighting, spell effects, environmental motion, and accessible visual alternatives. A plain text thread beside a diagnostic grid cannot pass.
39. Use original or properly licensed assets only. Enforce provider, license, attribution, trademark, logo, and generated-asset provenance gates.
40. Implement Google Sign-In as the only player-facing identity provider with the Phase 4 Invite-Only Alpha access package, reject temporary local identities from every hosted build, and rerun final provider and identity certification in Phase 7.
41. Escalate only for the explicit V1 human-authority conditions.
42. Stop at a human gate by freezing the candidate and creating an authenticated review checkpoint. Never infer approval from silence.
43. Advance only when the actual running product, required automated evidence, Builder page self-play, QA page validation, and any explicit human gate support the phase certificate. Separate independent challenge is additionally required for Phases 6 and 7.
44. Build the product rather than another plan about building the product.

The controlling standard is:

> Complete greenfield code, deterministic authority, rich player-facing presentation, executed evidence, honest failures, autonomous remediation, and no invented success.

## C.INTEGRITY — AI IMPLEMENTATION AGENT NON-DECEPTION CONTRACT

## C.INTEGRITY.1 Purpose

This appendix exists because an autonomous coding agent can produce convincing evidence of progress while leaving the actual user lifecycle disconnected. The agent must be evaluated by observable product behavior and canonical evidence, not by confidence, prose, screenshots of isolated components, or the number of files changed.

## C.INTEGRITY.2 Prohibited success claims

An implementation agent may not claim a requirement is complete because:

- The project compiles.
- Type checking passes.
- A component renders in isolation.
- A mocked service returned the expected object.
- A unit test exercised the agent’s own implementation assumptions.
- A screenshot resembles the design.
- A database document exists.
- A WebSocket says connected.
- An AI response contains valid-looking JSON.
- A button can be clicked.
- A local development environment worked once.
- The agent manually edited test data to reach the expected screen.
- An administrator bypass was used.
- A hidden feature flag disabled the difficult path.
- Another AI said the plan looked correct.

## C.INTEGRITY.3 Required completion statement

For every completed requirement, the agent must report:

- Requirement identifier.
- Files and services changed.
- Data and authority boundaries affected.
- Automated tests added.
- Local rendered-page black-box scenario that proves the player behavior when the requirement is player-facing.
- Failure scenario tested.
- Canonical evidence location.
- Accessibility evidence where relevant.
- Security evidence where relevant.
- Known limitations.
- Whether QA has certified it and whether a separate deep independent challenge was required for this phase/risk.

If any field is missing, the requirement status is Implemented but Unverified, not Complete.

## C.INTEGRITY.4 Mock discipline

Mocks are permitted for isolated development and deterministic test setup. They are not permitted in phase-certification paths unless the phase explicitly tests a component before its dependency exists and the UI unmistakably labels the data as simulated.

Before phase certification, the candidate must include a build-time and runtime check that rejects test-only authentication, fixed dice, fake payment, fake AI, sample ownership, admin bypass, or permissive security configuration in production.

## C.INTEGRITY.5 Test independence

QA Player Simulator must receive player goals, not implementation hints. It should not be told which selector IDs to click unless testing automation requires them after a manual usability run. The first run should discover the interface as a player would.

When a separate Independent QA Judge is required in Phase 6, Phase 7, or by a risk trigger, that judge must not share conversation state with the implementation agent or the QA Player Simulator. It receives only the blueprint, candidate manifest, raw evidence, and explicit claims.

## C.INTEGRITY.6 Evidence falsification controls

Screenshots and videos must show candidate deployment identity and time. Logs and events must carry correlation identifiers visible in the evidence package. Test accounts and campaigns must be newly created or reset through documented setup, not silently prearranged to avoid edge cases.

A test runner must not modify production-like state through direct database access after the scenario begins. Any fixture setup is recorded before the first player action.

## C.INTEGRITY.7 Requirement traceability

Every requirement has one of these states:

- Proposed.
- Approved.
- In Design.
- In Implementation.
- Implemented but Unverified.
- Candidate Verified.
- Phase Certified.
- Production Verified.
- Deprecated.
- Blocked.

Only Phase Certified or Production Verified requirements may be described as complete in roadmap summaries.

## C.INTEGRITY.8 Defect handling

A defect report must contain observed behavior, expected behavior, reproduction steps, candidate identifier, account and campaign context, evidence, severity, affected requirements, and whether state corruption occurred.

A defect is not closed because code changed. The original scenario must pass on a new frozen candidate and QA must inspect the regression evidence. During Phase 6/7 deep challenge, the Independent QA Judge additionally reviews high and critical defect closure.

## C.INTEGRITY.9 No silent scope reduction

An agent may discover that a phase is too broad. It may propose a narrower phase, but it cannot remove requirements, browser support, accessibility behavior, rules coverage, or failure cases without an approved change record. A partially implemented system must be labeled partial.

## C.INTEGRITY.10 No inferred user happiness

The agent may not infer fun or usability from technical success. Fun and usability claims require player behavior, surveys, interviews, or observed task completion. Telemetry may identify friction but cannot alone prove enjoyment.

## C.INTEGRITY.11 Agent Context Diet and Builder subagent contract

The implementation process must avoid two opposite failures:

- **Context starvation:** an agent lacks a relevant invariant or interface and guesses.
- **Context flooding:** an agent receives so much unrelated material that attention degrades and important requirements are effectively invisible.

Builder is accountable for both.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.1 Master authority versus working context

The Master Blueprint remains the final product authority and is never split into independent competing specifications. Modularization creates derived working packs, not new sources of truth.

Builder loads the required authority set, compiles packs when useful, and records source hashes. A subagent receives the Shared Invariant Kernel plus only the relevant domain, phase, code, tests, and interfaces. If an agent needs more, it requests a Context Expansion. It does not improvise.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.2 Context-pack folder and registry

The repository must contain a version-controlled context-pack registry with:

- Pack identifiers and role names.
- Source blueprint version.
- Source requirement identifiers.
- Source artifact hashes.
- Included domain files.
- Excluded domains.
- Allowed code paths.
- Required output artifacts.
- Required tests.
- Expiration triggers.
- Approval status.

Generated packs may live as build artifacts rather than hand-maintained duplicated prose, but the registry and compiler inputs are reviewable. A hand-edited pack cannot silently drift from its sources.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.3 Required subagent separation

At minimum, implementation orchestration separates these concerns when they are active in a phase:

- Architecture and context compilation.
- Frontend UI and accessibility.
- Map/rendering/effects.
- Deterministic rules and conformance.
- Realtime command lifecycle and persistence.
- AI intent, adjudication, narration, and policy.
- Security and authorization review.
- Browser/player simulation.
- Independent QA judgment when Phase 6/7 or a risk trigger requires a separate deep challenge.

These are logical concerns, not a mandate to spawn one subagent per bullet. A capable Builder may cover multiple implementation concerns in one context when ownership and attention remain clear. QA remains write-isolated from Builder source. When an Independent QA Judge is required, the implementation agent and that judge may never be the same logical agent or share hidden conversation state.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.4 Interface-first delegation

Before parallel Builder subagents write code, Builder freezes the interfaces they share:

- Input and output schemas.
- Ownership and authority.
- Error and timeout states.
- Versioning and compatibility.
- Performance budget.
- Test fixtures.
- Version transition responsibility.

A frontend agent may mock a frozen projection interface during isolated development, but phase certification uses the real hosted backend. A backend agent may publish a contract fixture, but it cannot declare the visual experience complete.

When an interface changes, dependent packs expire. Builder republishes them and either rebases or discards stale subagent work. “The other agent probably handled it” is not an integration plan.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.5 Context exclusion is explicit

Every pack states what it intentionally excludes. Example:

- Frontend action-tray pack excludes raw SRD extraction archives, audio mastering procedures, and account-deletion operations.
- Rules-engine pack excludes portrait prompt templates and layout spacing tables but includes projection fields and player-facing explanation requirements that the engine must produce.
- Audio pack excludes authentication implementation but includes event authority, hidden-information restrictions, and reconnect replay rules.

The exclusion list helps reviewers detect accidental omissions and stops agents from assuming absence means freedom.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.6 No hidden persistent-agent authority

Builder Root instructions, agent definitions, skills, memories, and automation files must be inventoried. They may improve consistency, but they may not contain undisclosed requirements, credentials, production bypasses, or rules that conflict with the blueprint.

Each persistent instruction artifact has:

- Owner.
- Purpose.
- Allowed agent roles.
- Version.
- Review date.
- Source requirements.
- Security classification.
- Retirement procedure.

A task is reproducible from version-controlled project artifacts. It must not depend on a developer’s private agent history.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.7 Tool and permission diet

Context limitation is paired with tool limitation. Each subagent receives only the repository paths, cloud environments, secrets scope, browser surfaces, databases, and commands required for its role.

- UI agents do not receive production database write credentials.
- Rules agents do not receive asset-generation billing keys unless required.
- QA agents receive test identities and evidence access, not implementation merge authority.
- Builder cannot use a broad credential to hide missing least-privilege design.
- Production access is not granted merely because an agent can complete the task faster with it.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.8 Subagent completion package

A subagent returns:

- Requirement identifiers addressed.
- Files changed.
- Interfaces consumed or changed.
- Tests run and raw results.
- Assumptions made.
- Context expansions requested.
- Known limitations.
- Security and accessibility effects.
- Version transition or rollback needs.
- Evidence locations.
- Questions or conflicts for Builder integration.

Builder reviews the package against the pack, integrates changes, runs cross-domain tests, and rejects unsupported success claims.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.9 Context-related failure conditions

A phase fails when:

- A relevant requirement was absent from the responsible pack.
- A subagent guessed across an excluded boundary instead of requesting expansion.
- Two subagents implemented incompatible versions of an interface.
- A stale pack remained active after a source change.
- Builder attached the full blueprint to every narrow subtask without a role plan and called that context management.
- A pack paraphrased away a hard requirement.
- An agent changed files outside its allowed scope without approval.
- QA lacked the authoritative requirement needed to judge the change.
- The process cannot reproduce which context an agent used.

### C.INTEGRITY.11.10 Context-diet certification evidence

The phase evidence package includes:

- Builder Phase Context Receipt.
- Each Role Context Pack and receipt.
- Pack compiler output and coverage report.
- Expansion requests.
- File-ownership plan.
- Subagent completion packages.
- Merge conflict and interface-drift review.
- QA sampling from blueprint to pack to implementation to test.
- Token/context budget report without exposing private chain-of-thought.

The report records input size, pack size, repository material loaded, tool-output volume, and truncation warnings. It does not request or preserve hidden reasoning.

## C.INTEGRITY.12 Local-development non-deception contract

An agent may not claim:

- “Tested locally” when any canonical data dependency reached production.
- “QA independent” when QA edited source or Builder edited QA expectations.
- “Frozen candidate” when hot reload, an unclean tree, or source changes continued.
- “Firebase emulator” when the UI was local but Firestore, Auth, Storage, Functions, or Admin SDK used live services.
- “Product Owner approved” without an authorization bound to the exact candidate and operation.
- “Phase deployed successfully” as a substitute for phase QA.
- “Clean test” without baseline and cleanup evidence.

The completion report must identify the local candidate, local stack, QA target, evidence root, unresolved defects, Product Owner authorization if any, remote identities if published, and production smoke result if performed.


## C.INTEGRITY.13 Quality-first execution and anti-token-laziness contract

Builder must not treat fast conversational completion as the work product. Before a phase handoff it must complete the Phase Requirement Ledger, real implementation, required focused/integration tests, actual-page self-play, smoke spine, impact-based regression, and required evidence. Deep challenge/full cumulative regression are added in Phases 6 and 7 or when risk requires them earlier.

When context pressure rises, Builder writes a durable checkpoint and resumes through a fresh scoped context pack. It does not remove requirements, insert placeholders, shorten matrices, or summarize failures into success. Progress telemetry records implementation-test-fix cycles, tests executed before the first readiness attempt, changed files after the last regression, skipped or flaky tests, and Builder escapes later found by QA. The telemetry measures rigor and detects rushing patterns; it does not reward slow execution for its own sake.

## C.INTEGRITY.14 Complete-code and no-placeholder contract

Every in-scope phase requirement must use complete local code through the real execution path. A requirement cannot be certified by a prototype, skeleton, happy-path approximation, fake button, hardcoded response, unresolved mock, direct database shortcut, TODO, or handler that conceals missing work.

The implementation agent reviews the actual saved files and produces a Code Completeness Scan. Future-phase work remains absent or explicitly isolated; it cannot be exposed as apparently working behavior or become a hidden dependency of current-phase certification.

## C.INTEGRITY.15 No-made-up-success and evidence-attestation contract

Success is a property of executed behavior, not authored language. Authoritative evidence is generated by the actual runner or trusted wrapper, bound to the frozen candidate, reconciled to the expected test and matrix manifests, and hash-sealed after completion.

Markdown summaries and phase reports are generated from raw evidence. They are not accepted as evidence. The evidence attestor verifies command execution, candidate identity, expected discovery, assertion execution, exit status, result counts, artifact presence, hashes, matrix reconciliation, and absence of stale or edited results.

If an agent claims success for a test that did not run, the event is a Critical Process Integrity Defect. The candidate’s complete verification package is invalid, even when the underlying code later appears correct.


## C.INTEGRITY.16 Holistic product and visual-completeness non-deception contract

An implementation agent may not claim the product is complete because individual components compile, a map JSON exists, a logo image exists, or a chat flow works.

The agent must demonstrate the integrated player experience across landing, login, character selection, campaign entry, visual stage, action, narration, persistence, reconnect, and return. It may not:

- Call a diagnostic grid a finished map.
- Call generic circles final tokens.
- Call a text transcript a complete tabletop.
- Call raw generated lettering a cleared logo.
- Call fog secure when secret assets were downloaded.
- Call a mocked provider a completed integration.
- Call fallback art the full visual tier.
- Call an unreviewed generated image original or licensed.
- Call a quick-start template complete when it bypasses normal character validation or ownership.

Every visual and provider claim requires candidate-bound evidence and the **specific reviewer/approval actor required by the governing core section**; ordinary Builder/QA review must not be silently upgraded into a Product Owner gate.

## C.CONTEXT — ROLE CONTEXT PACK MATRIX AND INTERRUPT TEST CATALOG

This appendix gives Builder a minimum operational matrix. It does not replace the requirement graph or authorize a subagent to ignore an interface referenced by its task.

## C.CONTEXT.1 Pack naming and identity

Each pack identifier contains:

- Blueprint major version.
- Phase.
- Candidate identifier.
- Role.
- Task identifier.
- Pack revision.

A pack is immutable after a subagent begins work. Corrections produce a new revision and invalidate the earlier receipt.

## C.CONTEXT.2 Shared invariant kernel contents

The kernel must fit as a compact standalone artifact and include direct requirement references for:

- Account identity and character ownership.
- Seat and command authorization.
- Hard invariants and Director ruling envelope.
- Command acceptance and interrupt-safe lifecycle.
- Idempotency and preserved randomness.
- Canonical Projection Binding.
- Hidden-information safety.
- Square-grid topology.
- Intent Intercept.
- Mechanics-first event presentation.
- Narrative streaming non-authority.
- Design and render registries.
- Accessibility and no-install rules.
- Policy, originality, and age boundary.
- Evidence and regression obligations.

## C.CONTEXT.3 Minimum role matrix

| Role | Must receive | Normally excluded | Mandatory output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Builder coordination | Full blueprint or phase-authoritative source set, decisions, schemas, certificates, repo inventory, open defects | May omit large raw assets and unrelated future-phase detail | Current-phase scope map, pack set when used, file ownership, dependency graph, aggregate receipt |
| Frontend UI | Kernel, design system, render registry, projections, action UX, intercept, accessibility, phase tests | Raw rules extraction, unrelated persistence internals, asset mastering | Accessible components, state matrix, browser tests, visual evidence |
| Map/Rendering | Kernel, square grid, map schema, visibility projection, templates, effects, layers | Account admin flows, broad narrative memory | Renderer, geometry presentation, input routing, visual regression evidence |
| Rules Engine | Kernel, SRD subset, deterministic rules, commands/events, randomness, ruling envelope, conformance tests | Portrait/audio prompts, marketing layout | Deterministic calculations, source traceability, golden and property tests |
| Realtime Backend | Kernel, auth-derived seat, lifecycle, persistence, outbox, reconnect, schemas, chaos tests | Detailed art direction, narrative prose style | Durable state machine, transport, recovery evidence, security tests |
| AI Orchestration | Kernel, intent/intercept, adjudication, narration stream, memory, policy, models, fallbacks | Canonical mutation authority, broad admin credentials | Structured prompts/contracts, evaluations, safety and latency evidence |
| Effects/Audio | Kernel, committed event taxonomy, layers, sound authority, accessibility, provenance | Character ownership internals except event audience | Event-bound assets, fallbacks, performance and sensory tests |
| Security Reviewer | Kernel plus full affected trust boundaries, endpoints, schemas, dependencies, agent permissions | Decorative assets unless attack-relevant | Threat findings, exploit evidence, remediation verification |
| QA Player Simulator | Player goals, scenario setup, public UX, acceptance criteria | Implementation plan and shortcuts | Raw run evidence, defects, observable pass/fail |
| Independent QA Judge | Authoritative requirements, receipts, candidate manifest, raw evidence, defects | Private implementation-agent conversation | Challenge report, rerun requests, final judgment |

## C.CONTEXT.4 Pack invalidation triggers

A pack expires when any of these changes:

- Blueprint version or affected requirement.
- Shared Invariant Kernel.
- Consumed interface schema.
- Rules-manifest record.
- Design System Manifest or Render Layer Registry used by the task.
- Security or authorization matrix.
- Candidate branch or major repository refactor.
- Phase exit criteria.
- Defect classified high or critical against the task.

Builder may declare a source change non-impacting only through a recorded dependency decision that QA may challenge during validation.

## C.CONTEXT.5 Interrupt test catalog

For each state-changing command category—movement, attack, save, spell, item, object, reaction, rest, social commitment, join, leave, departure-handling action—the harness should run the applicable interruption points from Section 25.6.

The minimum matrix crosses:

- Lifecycle state.
- Client fault.
- Server/worker fault.
- AI fault.
- Persistence conflict.
- Retry source.
- Number of connected clients.
- Active-turn ownership.
- Hidden-information presence.

A representative release suite must include at least:

1. Unconfirmed natural-language draft plus browser close.
2. Confirmed movement plus socket loss before baseline resolution.
3. Attack plus worker termination after random roll.
4. Spell plus Firestore contention before commit.
5. Reaction plus reconnect from another device.
6. Multi-target effect plus duplicate worker completion.
7. Committed critical hit plus narrative timeout.
8. Narrative stream plus out-of-order and duplicate chunks.
9. Voluntary leave while accepted action resolves.
10. Host disconnect while another player’s action resolves.
11. Cross-instance projection delay with two observers.
12. Optional effect asset failure after commit.

## C.CONTEXT.6 Latency evidence timeline

Every sampled consequential action records correlated timestamps for:

- Local input.
- Client send.
- Server receive.
- Intent interpretation complete.
- Intercept shown.
- Player confirmation.
- Accepted command.
- Baseline complete.
- Director adjudication complete.
- Commit complete.
- First projection received.
- Effect start.
- Mechanical summary visible.
- Narrative request start.
- First validated chunk.
- Final narrative stored.
- Delivery acknowledgement.

The evidence package reports p50, p95, p99, failure rate, fallback rate, and player-reported uncertainty. Performance claims without correlated lifecycle timestamps are insufficient.

## C.CONTEXT.7 Final process directive

For every parent work item, Builder records any Context Expansions and why they were needed in the Role Context Pack receipt. Subagents must treat Cinematic Final-Step Adjustment, Safe Disposition Candidate, Narrative Consequence Descriptor, and Improvised Action Potency Profile as shared interface contracts owned by designated integration agents. Narrow implementation agents may consume these contracts but may not locally redefine them.

For every phase:

1. Builder reads the current phase authority set and any directly affected prior contracts.
2. Builder compiles narrow packs when the selected tooling/task benefits from them; a single-context Builder may instead use the current phase execution pack directly.
3. If Builder uses subagents, each subagent acknowledges scope and missing context.
4. Interfaces are frozen before parallel work only when parallel subagents share an interface; sequential single-context work does not need a ceremonial freeze.
5. If subagents are used, they implement only within assigned scope.
6. Builder integrates any delegated work and runs cross-domain tests.
7. QA simulates real players, including interruption and latency scenarios.
8. QA tries to disprove the player-facing result; a separate Independent QA Judge is added only for Phase 6, Phase 7, or an earlier risk trigger.
9. The permanent smoke spine and impact-selected prior regression run on the same frozen local candidate served by the Local Arena; Phase 6 and Phase 7 run the full cumulative suite.
10. A human reviews only the explicit visual, safety, legal, publication, or Launch Production gates owned by that phase; ordinary local phase progress does not require a recurring human certificate.

The objective is not to make the AI read less for its own comfort. The objective is to make the correct requirements more salient, the boundaries more explicit, and the proof harder to fake.

## C.CONTEXT.8 Runtime-root and local-target context contract

Every Builder Role Context Pack names `<WORKING_DIRECTORY>/Builder` as its writable project root. Every QA pack names `<WORKING_DIRECTORY>/QA` as its writable project root. Both roles may receive read-only references to the other role’s permitted artifacts; neither pack grants cross-role write authority.

Context packs include:

- Canonical root and sentinel identity.
- Local candidate URL and Local Stack Manifest identity.
- Allowed external origins.
- Production-target prohibition.
- Rapid Builder or Frozen Certification mode.
