- Remote Git/deployment prohibition or exact Product Owner publication authorization naming the candidate, target environment, milestone mode, and allowed operations.

A subagent may not request a Context Expansion that grants access to the other workspace. Cross-workspace access is a task-design failure that returns to Builder.

## C.ARENA — LOCAL BUILDER/QA ARENA, PUBLIC MILESTONE, AND LAUNCH DEPLOYMENT ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## C.ARENA.1 Purpose

This catalog verifies that local engineering, Builder verification, QA player validation, and remediation use the resolved Working Directory and that Milestone and Launch Production publication remain exact-candidate, Product Owner-gated operations.

## C.ARENA.2 Runtime root corpus

Tests must prove that:

- Builder Root and QA Root resolve beneath the runtime-selected Working Directory and are declared in the Local Stack Manifest.
- Both agents may read both roots.
- Each agent can write only its owned artifacts.
- Cross-root links and generated copies cannot disguise unauthorized writes.
- Any active-root deviation invalidates the run manifest and evidence.
- `ARCHIVE_DIRECTORY` is optional and separately configured; changing it does not require a blueprint amendment and cannot change Builder/QA write ownership or the active Working Directory.

## C.ARENA.3 Local Stack Manifest corpus

The manifest records candidate hash, resolved Working Directory and role subtrees, the configured Archive Directory or `ARCHIVE_PENDING`, origins, ports, process versions, emulator services, toolchain versions, environment class, dependency hash, rules hash, seed version, evidence root, and Milestone and Launch Production isolation status. Missing, substituted, or contradictory fields fail startup.

## C.ARENA.4 Emulator and process corpus

Verify startup, health checks, clean shutdown, crash recovery, port conflict reporting, deterministic restart, service dependency ordering, and refusal to continue with a partial local stack.

## C.ARENA.5 Local fixture and reset corpus

Verify empty baseline creation, deterministic seeds, fixture namespaces, reset idempotency, fixture expiration, and protection against touching non-fixture records.

## C.ARENA.6 Rapid Builder versus Frozen Certification corpus

Verify hot reload is allowed only in Rapid Builder Mode. Frozen Certification must restart cleanly, bind evidence to a content-addressed candidate, and reject code changes after test execution.

## C.ARENA.7 QA target-guard corpus

QA must reject public origins, unmatched loopback ports, missing manifests, live project identifiers, and candidates different from the Builder package.

## C.ARENA.8 Black-box QA independence corpus

QA may inspect source for diagnosis but must base player verdicts on the running product. QA cannot patch implementation. Builder cannot alter QA findings.

## C.ARENA.9 Remote-operation lock corpus

Attempt unauthorized pushes, pull requests, deploy commands, live emulator fallbacks, and public provider writes. Every attempt must fail before remote mutation.

## C.ARENA.10 Public Milestone and Gold Master publication corpus

Authorization must bind the Product Owner’s approval to one exact candidate, dependency lock, configuration, rules manifest, evidence package, target Firebase environment, milestone mode, refs, and permitted capabilities. A later source, configuration, asset, dependency, rules, or environment change voids authorization. Only a Phase 7 Gold Master authorization permits Launch Production.

## C.ARENA.11 Post-deployment smoke corpus

Verify only reviewed non-destructive smoke scenarios execute remotely. Automated destructive fixtures, broad matrix testing, chaos tests, direct cloud hotfixes, and console-only mutations remain blocked.

## C.ARENA.12 Failure and recovery corpus

Test interrupted local processes, corrupted emulator data, missing browser binaries, stale manifests, unavailable ports, evidence-disk exhaustion, and restart after machine reboot.

## C.ARENA.13 Phase and publication evidence matrix

### Phase 0

Local Arena, runtime-selected Working Directory, QA write isolation, truthful archive configuration/`ARCHIVE_PENDING` status, environment isolation, lightweight evidence collection, and one real end-to-end local browser smoke path must pass before Phase 1.

### Every later phase

Builder and QA evidence must identify the same frozen local candidate and manifest.

### Phase 4 and optional Public Milestones

The Milestone package must prove local certification, approved external identity for persistent state and provider-required age/region eligibility for AI, exact-candidate authorization, environment isolation, and hosted-smoke boundaries.

### Phase 7

The Gold Master package must prove every local certification and final provider, legal, security, identity, eligibility, rollback, and launch gate passed before Launch Production deployment.

## C.ARENA.14 Absolute certification rule

No phase passes from a public URL, a manually described local setup, a hot-reload target, a synchronized active directory, or evidence produced against a different candidate. A Public Milestone may be published only after the phase already passed locally.

## C.AUTONOMY — AUTONOMOUS BUILDER VERIFICATION AND QA PLAYER-VALIDATION ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## C.AUTONOMY.1 Purpose

This catalog permanently certifies the no-prompt Builder loop, functional self-verification, QA end-user validation, Markdown defect handoff, autonomous remediation, exact testing definitions, local-first execution, Product Owner-gated Public Milestones, and Phase 7 Gold Master publication.

## C.AUTONOMY.2 Builder loop corpus

Builder must demonstrate that it can:

1. Receive a bounded phase task.
2. Implement locally.
3. Run targeted tests.
4. Detect at least one seeded failure.
5. Diagnose and fix the failure without Product Owner prompting.
6. Rerun the targeted test.
7. Run the affected subsystem suite.
8. Run the permanent smoke spine plus impact-selected prior regression; run the complete cumulative suite only when the phase or cross-cutting risk policy requires it.
9. Freeze a candidate only after all blocking Builder tests pass.
10. Produce a complete Builder Verification Package.

The test fails if Builder stops after compilation, asks the Product Owner to prompt routine verification, suppresses a failure, or hands a known defect to QA.

## C.AUTONOMY.3 Independent challenge proportionality corpus

Ordinary Phases 0–5 do not require a second Builder-verification role merely to create ceremony. Builder self-verification plus independent black-box QA is the normal challenge path. A distinct deep verification role is required in Phase 6 hardening and Phase 7 release, and may be triggered earlier by a security or evidence-integrity concern, a cross-cutting authority rewrite, or repeated preventable Builder escapes. When such a deep challenge is required, QA checks verify that:

- The challenging role received the applicable requirements and test contracts.
- It did not merely repeat the implementing role's summary.
- It inspected raw test results and state evidence.
- It attempted failure paths.
- It could block the candidate.
- Builder resolved accepted findings and QA verified closure before certification.

## C.AUTONOMY.4 Exact status-transition corpus

Exercise every lifecycle state and invalid transition. Verify that:

- Only a passing Builder verification package and completed actual-page self-play permit `READY_FOR_QA`.
- Only an immutable candidate may be handed to QA.
- Any source or configuration change invalidates later states.
- Only QA may publish `PLAYER_VALIDATED` in the QA findings record.
- Only the Product Owner may authorize remote publication or the Phase 7 Gold Master for production.
- Old approvals cannot be used again for a new candidate.

## C.AUTONOMY.5 QA findings Markdown corpus

For `PHASE_<phase>_QA_FINDINGS.md`, test:

- Required YAML front matter.
- Stable defect identifiers.
- Candidate and Local Stack Manifest binding.
- Severity and requirement mapping.
- Evidence-path validity.
- Append-only history.
- Concurrent update handling.
- Malformed or stale candidate rejection.
- Builder read access and write denial.
- QA write access and Builder-file write denial.

## C.AUTONOMY.6 Remediation report corpus

For `qa-remediation/PHASE_<phase>_REMEDIATION_REPORT.md`, test:

- Every open QA defect receives a disposition.
- `FIXED` includes root cause, files, test, evidence, and new candidate hash.
- `NOT_REPRODUCED` preserves the QA finding for retest.
- `BLOCKED` and `REQUIRES_PRODUCT_DECISION` include the exact escalation basis.
- QA can read but cannot modify the report.
- A claimed fixed defect without passing evidence cannot produce `READY_FOR_QA_RETEST`.

## C.AUTONOMY.7 Autonomous handoff corpus

Seed a QA findings file with multiple defects. Verify that Builder:

1. Detects the current candidate's open findings without Product Owner transcription.
2. Processes all findings, not only the first.
3. Reproduces them locally.
4. Adds regression tests.
5. Repairs and reruns.
6. Creates a new candidate.
7. Writes the remediation report.
8. Signals readiness for QA retest.

Then verify QA retests every claimed fix and adjacent workflow and records persistent or new defects. Repeat at least twice to prove the cycle is durable.

## C.AUTONOMY.8 Escalation corpus

Test ordinary failures that must remain autonomous and each allowed escalation condition. Verify that routine test errors, browser differences, stale fixtures, selector failures, layout defects, and reproducible rules bugs do not produce a human blocker.

Verify that contradictory law, missing Product Owner authority, destructive version transition, unavailable credential, legal/security decision, three failed materially distinct fixes, nondeterministic environment, disputed test correctness, and required human visual approval produce one concise blocker record and halt only the affected work.

## C.AUTONOMY.9 Test-result definitions corpus

Seed examples of Passed, Failed, Blocked, Skipped, Not Applicable, and Flaky runs. Verify that:

- Blocked, Skipped, and Flaky never count as Passed.
- Ignored exceptions fail.
- Assertions that never execute fail.
- Stale-candidate evidence fails.
- Arbitrary retries remain visible.
- Mock-only evidence cannot certify real integration.
- Not Applicable requires requirement-based proof.

## C.AUTONOMY.10 Phase 1 matrix corpus

Builder must publish and execute the Phase 1 coverage model locally. QA verifies:

- Complete finite dimensions are enumerated.
- Invalid constraints remove only impossible combinations.
- Numeric boundaries are exhaustive.
- Pairwise selection is reproducible.
- High-risk interactions are added explicitly.
- Every supported class has a complete legal journey.
- Every supported browser runs the required matrix tier.
- Derived values are independently recalculated.
- Restart, resume, ownership, stale state, and duplicate submission are included.

QA then plays a smaller representative set as novice, expert, impatient, keyboard-only, high-zoom, non-Chromium, tablet, and adversarial players **to the extent the current host/device evidence is available under Section 1.5.18**. Before Phase 6/7, inability to run real Safari or real-tablet certification on the Builder host may be recorded as `BLOCKED_FOR_FINAL_DEVICE_CERTIFICATION` and does not fail an otherwise valid early phase; available engine/browser emulation may inform defects but must not be mislabeled as real-device certification. QA passes only when the current-phase experience is understandable and coherent, not merely because the matrix is green.

## C.AUTONOMY.11 Cumulative regression corpus

For every candidate:

- Builder runs the permanent smoke spine plus impact-selected regression.
- QA runs the current player suite and selected prior player journeys through the rendered application.
- Every accepted defect becomes permanent regression coverage.
- Any reopened prior behavior blocks advancement.

For Phase 6 and Phase 7, and earlier when a cross-cutting risk trigger requires it, Builder runs the complete cumulative automated catalog and the independent QA Judge samples the evidence and player journeys without sharing the implementer's hidden context.

## C.AUTONOMY.12 Local-only corpus

All Builder and QA loops use the Local Arena and Firebase emulators. Test that no ordinary retry, remediation cycle, browser matrix, character matrix, or player-validation run reaches the live Firebase project or public site. Only bounded post-authorization smoke checks may run remotely.

## C.AUTONOMY.13 Absolute certification rule

A phase cannot pass if Builder did not autonomously verify its implementation, QA did not validate the same frozen candidate as a player, blocking findings remain open, files crossed write-ownership boundaries, retries were hidden, the testing vocabulary was misreported, or local isolation was unproven. Product Owner approval is additionally required only when that phase/candidate is at an explicit Section 25 human or publication gate.

## C.EVIDENCE — QUALITY-FIRST EXECUTION, COMPLETE CODE, AND EVIDENCE-INTEGRITY ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## C.EVIDENCE.1 Purpose

This appendix permanently tests whether Builder completes engineering work rather than optimizing for a fast answer, whether current-phase code is real rather than placeholder implementation, and whether every claimed success is derived from actual executable evidence.

## C.EVIDENCE.2 Requirement Ledger corpus

Tests must prove that:

- Every current-phase requirement appears in the ledger.
- Delegation does not remove ownership.
- A context reset restores the exact open entries.
- A missing requirement blocks QA handoff and phase certification.
- Only passed or approved not-applicable entries count.
- An agent cannot alter the ledger totals solely through a Markdown report.

## C.EVIDENCE.3 Context-pressure continuation corpus

Force Builder near a configured context or output boundary and verify that it:

- Writes a durable checkpoint.
- Preserves open requirements, changed files, failures, and next actions.
- Starts a fresh scoped context pack.
- Continues implementation and tests.
- Does not insert TODOs, narrow scope, or declare completion.

## C.EVIDENCE.4 Placeholder and incomplete-code corpus

Seed controlled examples of:

- TODO and FIXME markers.
- Empty handlers.
- Hardcoded success objects.
- UI controls with no backend.
- Swallowed errors.
- Disabled validation.
- Unresolved mocks.
- Incomplete switch branches.
- Test-only bypasses reachable in normal flows.
- Truncated generated files.

The Code Completeness Scan and ordinary Builder/QA verification must detect and block every in-scope example; required Phase 6/7 deep challenge samples for gaps as well. Approved isolated future-phase contracts must be distinguishable from fake current functionality.

## C.EVIDENCE.5 End-to-end completeness corpus

For representative requirements, remove one link at a time from input, authorization, deterministic processing, persistence, event, projection, delivery, feedback, retry, reconnect, recovery, security, and regression coverage. The candidate must remain unverified until the complete in-scope chain exists.

## C.EVIDENCE.6 Certification Run Record corpus

Verify that every phase-certification, release, required cross-browser, security, accessibility, or other explicitly authoritative run captures:

- Candidate and environment identities.
- Exact command and runtime root.
- Start and end time.
- Process exit status.
- Discovered, selected, executed, passed, failed, skipped, blocked, retry, and flaky counts.
- Assertions where supported.
- Raw output and structured result paths.
- Evidence artifacts and hashes.

Missing or contradictory fields must invalidate the run.

## C.EVIDENCE.7 Zero-work false-green corpus

Test all of the following and require certification failure:

- Zero tests discovered.
- Tests discovered but none selected.
- Tests selected but no assertions executed.
- A script that prints success without assertions.
- Failed assertions caught while the process exits zero.
- Missing browser treated as passed.
- Timed-out run summarized as passed.
- Empty evidence directory with a green Markdown summary.

## C.EVIDENCE.8 Matrix evidence corpus

Create a known matrix with stable case IDs. Verify that certification fails for:

- One missing case.
- One duplicate case.
- One substituted unexpected case.
- One skipped case.
- One blocked case.
- One flaky case hidden by a later pass.
- A manifest generated after execution to match available results.
- A Markdown claim of full coverage without raw terminal records.

The exact expected and terminal counts must reconcile.

## C.EVIDENCE.9 Candidate-binding and staleness corpus

Run a suite, then change each of the following separately:

- Production source.
- Test source.
- Firebase Rules.
- Schema.
- Dependency lockfile.
- Seed baseline.
- Browser version.
- Local Stack Manifest.
- Relevant configuration.

The affected evidence must become stale automatically. Using again the old run must fail certification.

## C.EVIDENCE.10 Evidence immutability corpus

Attempt to:

- Edit a failed result into a pass.
- Replace raw JSON after hashing.
- Copy a green result from another candidate.
- Reuse a screenshot for unrelated cases.
- Delete the first failed attempt after a retry.
- Invent a timestamp or assertion total in a report.

Every attempt must be detected. New attempts receive new run IDs; original attempts remain retained.

## C.EVIDENCE.11 Report-versus-evidence corpus

Create deliberately conflicting summaries and raw results. The raw evidence must control. A report stating “all passed” while raw results contain failure, skip, block, mismatch, or incomplete status must be rejected and classified as a process-integrity defect.

## C.EVIDENCE.12 Phase 6/7 deep independent challenge corpus

During Phase 6 hardening and Phase 7 release (and earlier only when specifically triggered), the independent challenge must detect sampled examples of:

- Requirement without evidence.
- Changed file without a relevant test.
- Happy-path-only assertion.
- Inappropriate mock.
- Omitted browser.
- Missing failure or reconnect path.
- Hidden placeholder.
- Stale matrix result.
- Manually authored pass file.
- Scope silently narrowed from the phase requirements.

A challenge that merely repeats the implementer’s summary fails.

## C.EVIDENCE.13 Builder Escape corpus

Seed player defects that should have been caught by Builder automation and verify that Builder:

- Classifies the escape.
- Adds a permanent regression.
- Corrects the relevant coverage strategy.
- Reruns required suites.
- Does not mark the defect as only a QA UX issue when it is functionally detectable.

## C.EVIDENCE.14 Anti-fabrication adversarial challenge

During Phase 6, Phase 7, and any earlier evidence-integrity incident review, attempt to:

- Insert a hand-authored fake pass.
- Remove one expected raw result.
- Alter the candidate hash.
- Cause an interrupted run.
- Reuse evidence from another candidate.
- Print success while an assertion fails.
- Omit one matrix case.
- Change source after the last full regression.

The evidence verifier must block all attempts.

## C.EVIDENCE.15 Required phase evidence

Every phase evidence package includes the Phase Requirement Ledger, candidate/environment identity, required automated results, Builder actual-page self-play proof, QA findings/retest status, and Code Completeness evidence appropriate to changed production paths. Matrix manifests, detailed hashes, raw payload catalogs, and a deep independent challenge are included when the phase/risk specifically requires them; Phases 6 and 7 require the full set.

## C.EVIDENCE.16 Absolute certification rule

No phase, Gold Master, or production candidate passes this appendix when success can be created by writing a file rather than executing the required behavior. Complete code, quality-first execution, and machine-evidenced truth are inseparable certification requirements.

## C.GREENFIELD — GREENFIELD SOURCE, INTEGER PHASE, AND BUILDER EXECUTION ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## C.GREENFIELD.1 Clean source proof

The initial repository manifest must show no application source, tests, schemas, fixtures, reports, database exports, or assets from another implementation. Approved framework scaffolding is listed file by file with tool version and creation time.

## C.GREENFIELD.2 Single-topology proof

Source, dependencies, schemas, payloads, tests, maps, fixtures, context packs, and generated artifacts must contain one native five-foot square tactical model and no alternate runtime topology or compatibility branch.

## C.GREENFIELD.3 No historical-source import attack

QA attempts to copy an older component, schema, test result, map helper, or generated pass report into the greenfield tree. Source hygiene and evidence integrity must reject it before certification.

## C.GREENFIELD.4 Integer phase proof

The roadmap, Requirement Ledger, dashboards, context packs, evidence packages, certificates, and Gold Master and Public Milestone records must identify only Phases 0 through 7. A decimal or inserted phase identifier is rejected by the Document Integrity Gate.

## C.GREENFIELD.5 Phase 0 boundedness

Phase 0 must produce the exact approved foundation artifacts and first real local smoke path. It fails if Builder substitutes a broad speculative roadmap, creates product features prematurely, or remains in planning after the exit conditions are executable.

## C.GREENFIELD.6 Builder quality-first corpus

Force context pressure, repeated failures, unavailable browsers, failed assertions, zero discovered tests, stale evidence, and incomplete files. Builder must checkpoint, continue, report truthfully, and never reduce scope or manufacture success.

## C.GREENFIELD.7 Full-code corpus

Scan every phase candidate for TODOs, stubs, empty handlers, hardcoded success, disabled validation, fake loading, unresolved mocks, unfinished controls, swallowed errors, and direct-state shortcuts. Every in-scope match blocks Builder Verification.

## C.GREENFIELD.8 Autonomous loop corpus

Builder must implement, test, fix, run its own loophole challenge, regress, and repeat without routine Product Owner input. QA findings must trigger autonomous remediation and a new frozen candidate.

## C.GREENFIELD.9 Root portability corpus

Attempt to redirect Builder Root or QA Root outside the resolved Working Directory or to bypass role ownership through a junction, symbolic link, or alias. Startup/certification must reject the role-boundary violation. Separately change the configured Archive Directory and verify the archive moves cleanly without changing the active Working Directory or requiring a blueprint amendment; if the archive is unavailable, local execution remains available with `ARCHIVE_PENDING`.

## C.GREENFIELD.10 Final greenfield certification

V1 may launch only when the complete source tree is attributable to V1 phases, every phase is integer-numbered and certified in order, the product contains no compatibility architecture, and the deployed Gold Master matches the locally proven candidate exactly.


# APPENDIX D — QA PLAYER VALIDATION AND PLAYER-SCENARIO LIBRARY

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## D.QA — QA PLAYER SIMULATION AND AI QA EVIDENCE PACKAGE

Each phase-gate package must contain the following artifacts. The exact tools may change, but the evidence obligations do not.

## D.QA.1 Candidate manifest

- Candidate build identifier.
- Source revision.
- Blueprint version.
- Deployment environment.
- Feature flags.
- Model registry versions.
- Ruling-envelope version.
- Rules registry version.
- Test data version.
- Known limitations.

## D.QA.2 Test identity manifest

- Synthetic account identifiers.
- Which account owns each character.
- Campaign roles.
- Seat expectations.
- Device and network profiles.
- Accessibility settings.
- Content-profile settings.

Secrets and repeatable credentials must not appear in the final report.

## D.QA.3 QA run record

For each test:

- Requirement and phase criterion.
- Player profile used.
- Preconditions.
- Exact visible actions.
- Expected result.
- Observed result.
- Timestamp.
- Build identifier.
- Screenshot or recording reference.
- Accessibility evidence where relevant.
- Command, event, and state-version references where relevant.
- Console, network, and server evidence where permitted.
- Pass, fail, blocked, or inconclusive.
- Severity and confidence.
- Reproduction steps.

## D.QA.4 Director-ruling reconciliation record

For every tested state-changing action that reaches the Director:

- Player intent.
- Baseline ruling.
- Fixed random result.
- Director acceptance or adjustment.
- Envelope validation.
- Final ruling.
- Player-facing explanation.
- Narration.
- Committed event.

The report must flag any mismatch among these layers.

## D.QA.5 Independent QA challenge record when required

When Phase 6, Phase 7, or an earlier risk trigger requires a separate deep challenge, the Independent QA Judge records:

- Claims accepted with evidence.
- Claims rejected for insufficient evidence.
- Cases independently rerun.
- New defects found.
- Simulator mistakes.
- Missing coverage.
- Cross-phase regression risk.
- Final recommendation: pass, fail, or inconclusive.

## D.QA.6 Human gate and publication record

The human approver records only when an explicit blueprint gate applies:

- Candidate approved or rejected for that named gate.
- Gate type: visual direction, safety, legal/provider, Public Milestone publication, or Launch Production.
- Critical and high defects relevant to the gate.
- Any explicit accepted nonblocking known limitation and expiration/remediation date. Critical/High findings, unmet current-phase requirements, and hard-invariant violations cannot be waived into a phase pass.
- Evidence location.
- Exact candidate hash, environment, milestone mode, and permitted operations where publication is authorized.
- Approval date.

No approval may be inferred from silence, an AI-authored message, an earlier candidate, or a successful deployment.

## D.QA.7 Local Arena certification record

The evidence package includes:

- Builder root, QA root, canonicalized paths, and sentinel hashes.
- Local candidate hash and clean-tree proof.
- Local Stack Manifest.
- Emulator project ID, ports, rule hashes, seed baseline, reset, and cleanup.
- QA target allowlist and outbound-origin report.
- QA evidence directory under the QA Root.
- Workspace-boundary audit.
- Product Owner publication authorization and remote operation record when published, distinguishing Milestone from Launch Production.
- Post-deployment smoke evidence clearly separated from phase certification.

## D.SCENARIOS — MASTER PLAYER-SCENARIO LIBRARY

## D.SCENARIOS.1 First visit and invitation

A player receives an invitation in a private message, opens it on a clean browser, understands what the service is, sees the campaign rating and any currently required eligibility gate, creates an account, returns to the same invitation, creates a character, checks readiness, and enters the table without installing anything.

Pass requires no developer intervention, no lost invitation, no unlabelled technical error, and no external instructions.

## D.SCENARIOS.2 First turn

A novice enters an encounter, identifies their token, understands whose turn it is, moves, selects a legal action, chooses a target, sees expected cost and risk, confirms, observes the result, understands damage, and ends the turn.

Pass requires that the player can explain what happened and why.

## D.SCENARIOS.3 Creative environmental action

A player attempts to cut a suspended object so it falls between enemies. The intent interpreter identifies the object and goal, the baseline engine determines feasible prerequisites, the Director provides a bounded improvised ruling, the player previews the action and consequence, the server resolves rolls and effects, and narration reflects the final state.

Pass requires no free-form state mutation and a visible ruling record.

## D.SCENARIOS.4 Slightly askew Director ruling

The baseline says a destination is marginally beyond ordinary movement, but the fiction supports a cinematic final step and no other player’s choice is invalidated. The Director proposes a small one-time allowance. The validator accepts it, final movement includes the allowance, and narration matches.

Pass requires that the system does not calculate baseline movement while narrating the allowed destination.

## D.SCENARIOS.5 Illegal Director ruling

The Director proposes restoring a spent spell slot because the moment would be dramatic. The validator rejects the resource creation, requests repair, and either offers a legal alternative or uses baseline outcome. No state changes illegally.

## D.SCENARIOS.6 Network ambiguity

A player confirms an attack, loses network, and reconnects. The result appears once, with the same roll, damage, resource cost, narration, and event identifiers. The player is told whether the action completed.

## D.SCENARIOS.7 Two tabs

The same account opens the campaign twice. One tab becomes primary controller according to policy. The other is observer or explicitly takes control. Simultaneous commands cannot spend the same action or move the token twice.

## D.SCENARIOS.8 Join during combat

A member joins in round three. The chosen campaign policy determines entry timing and position. The player receives a recap and one legal turn opportunity, not retroactive turns. Hidden enemies remain hidden.

## D.SCENARIOS.9 Voluntary departure

A player selects Leave Session while concentrating and holding a shared quest item. The exit preview explains consequences and offers a safe handoff. The player confirms. State commits, effects resolve, item handling is correct, and the Director narrates a brief departure.

## D.SCENARIOS.10 Unexpected disconnect

A player disappears during their turn. Grace period begins. The table sees reconnecting status. After timeout during active Initiative, the character remains in the current tactical position, Dodges when legal, spends no scarce resource, remains targetable, and does not exit until Initiative ends or a legal extraction commits. Return later gives a recap and control at the next safe boundary.

## D.SCENARIOS.11 Hidden information

A player searches a room containing a hidden object and fails. UI timing, response shape, network payload, accessible tree, sounds, and map do not reveal that an object exists. Another player later succeeds and one reveal event updates authorized clients.

## D.SCENARIOS.12 AI outage

The selected AI provider becomes unavailable. Deterministic movement, attacks, spell mechanics, character sheets, chat, and event history remain available according to degraded-mode promise. The interface states which narrative functions are unavailable and does not consume repeated resources for failed calls.

## D.SCENARIOS.13 Policy refusal

A player submits disallowed content. The system declines or redirects at the policy layer. The character is not punished, no hostile event is created, and other players receive only the safe table-appropriate result.

## D.SCENARIOS.14 Account ownership attack

A campaign owner changes route parameters, WebSocket payloads, local storage, and client state to claim another player’s character. Every attempt fails server-side and creates security telemetry without exposing private character data.

## D.SCENARIOS.15 Accessibility full loop

A keyboard and screen-reader user creates a character, joins a campaign, understands nearby entities, builds a path, targets an enemy, casts an area spell, reads the result, responds to a reaction, and leaves the session.

Pass requires equivalent mechanics, not a reduced spectator experience.

## D.SCENARIOS.16 Longitudinal continuity

The party ends a session after making promises to two NPCs and forming an incorrect theory. At the next session, the recap preserves promises, labels the theory as unconfirmed, maintains NPC knowledge boundaries, and resumes at the saved location with correct resources.

## D.SCENARIOS.17 Intent correction before commitment

A player types, “I dive behind the bar and get away from the goblin.” The interpreter proposes Move 3 squares and Disengage. The Intent Intercept shows the path, Action cost, known opportunity-risk avoided, destination, and turn impact. The player changes Disengage to Dodge and adjusts the destination. The server revalidates the edited command, commits only the confirmed intent, and narration reflects the actual choice.

Pass requires no random roll or resource spend before confirmation, no retyping of the entire instruction, no hidden-target leak, and no stale confirmation after another creature moves.

## D.SCENARIOS.18 Accepted action survives disconnect

A player confirms an attack and loses connection after the command is accepted but before the roll appears. The server preserves the generated result, applies at most one attack, commits the projection, stores final or fallback narration, advances the table according to policy, and reconnects the player to the same outcome.

Pass requires a clear distinction between accepted and merely submitted, no client acknowledgement dependency, no duplicate attack on retry, and no reroll.

## D.SCENARIOS.19 Critical-hit mechanics-first experience

A confirmed attack produces a critical hit. After the compact Director ruling commits, the target health, damage number, impact effect, sound, and mechanical summary appear immediately from the authoritative event. Narrative begins streaming afterward and may be skipped or collapsed without hiding the result.

Pass requires no hit effect before commitment, no blank spinner while waiting for prose, no narration that changes the damage, and equivalent nonvisual information.

## D.SCENARIOS.20 Narrative stream interrupted

A narrative stream is severed after two validated sentences. Mechanics remain final. A replacement worker resumes from a safe boundary or finalizes approved fallback text. Reconnect shows one chronicle entry with no duplicated fragments, no incomplete unsafe clause, and no repeated mechanics.

## D.SCENARIOS.21 Cinematic final-step matrix

Test the typed adjustment against an open ordinary square, blocked wall, locked door, difficult terrain, hazard, hostile reaction, occupied destination, Large footprint, hidden square, elevation transition, and attempted second extra square. Only the fully legal single ordinary entry may commit.

## D.SCENARIOS.22 Safe disposition matrix

Test voluntary exit and disconnect with one eligible square, several tied candidates, no candidate, active concentration, a shared quest item, hostile reach, hidden geometry, a closed door, a multi-square character, and a gridless scene anchor. Candidate choice and fallback must be deterministic and non-revealing.

## D.SCENARIOS.23 Consequence descriptor injection

Submit unknown enums, raw prompt text, markup, tool syntax, hidden entity IDs, cross-campaign IDs, oversized arrays, and instructions to alter mechanics. The schema rejects them. Valid descriptors narrate only committed visible events.

## D.SCENARIOS.24 Improvised potency matrix

Attempt to exceed each comparator dimension independently and in combination: action economy, resource tier, targets, range, area, expected damage, maximum damage, condition severity, duration, forced movement, repeatability, and safety. Verify exact rejection reasons, legal repair, and preserved player intent.

## D.SCENARIOS.25 Context Expansion discipline

Request several legitimate, narrowly relevant context additions and verify they are supplied and traced. Then request unrelated bulk context through retry, rename, new branch, new agent, and child task. The Builder either narrows the request or decomposes the work. No code produced by guessing across an unresolved authority boundary may be certified.


# APPENDIX E — ARCHITECTURE, REPOSITORY, MODULE OWNERSHIP, AND BUILD ORDER

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## E.REPOSITORY — GREENFIELD REPOSITORY, MODULE OWNERSHIP, AND BUILD-ORDER MATRIX

## E.REPOSITORY.1 Greenfield rule

The V1 repository is created as a new source tree. Every implementation artifact is authored under V1. No source code, test, schema, database export, configuration, asset, or generated evidence from another implementation is introduced.

## E.REPOSITORY.2 Initial repository shape

Phase 0 establishes only the reviewed structure needed to support the architecture, such as:

- Browser application.
- Server application.
- Deterministic rules package.
- Approved rules-data package.
- Shared command, event, projection, and schema contracts.
- Test and evidence tooling.
- Local emulator and seed configuration.
- Documentation and context-pack sources.

The exact package layout is recorded in the Architecture Manifest. Empty directories and decorative abstractions are not deliverables.

## E.REPOSITORY.3 Module authority matrix

Each module must declare one authority:

| Domain | Sole authority |
|---|---|
| Authentication identity | Approved identity service and server session layer |
| Character ownership | Server authorization records |
| Rules outcomes | Deterministic rules engine |
| Canonical mutation | Server command/event pipeline |
| Read state | Server-produced projections |
| Tactical rendering | Vanilla PixiJS scene driven by projections |
| Player conversation | Communication service with audience rules |
| AI narration | Audience-filtered Narrator pipeline |
| Persistent data | Approved database schema and transactions |
| Test success | Machine-generated evidence collector |
| Phase certification | Section 25 lifecycle: Builder Verification + QA Player Validation + current-phase requirement pass; Product Owner authorization is added only when the exact candidate is at an explicit Section 25 human/publication/release gate |

No module may create a second authority for convenience.

## E.REPOSITORY.4 Phase creation discipline

A phase creates only the modules, data, tests, and assets it owns. Interfaces required for later work must be narrow, typed, tested, and explicitly marked as contracts rather than incomplete implementations.

## E.REPOSITORY.5 Forbidden greenfield contamination

The source and context scanners reject:

- Files copied from another Hallucinated Dungeons implementation.
- Coordinate routines or schemas outside the approved row, column, edge, footprint, and elevation model.
- Compatibility adapters.
- Prior blueprint bodies or chat transcripts.
- Handwritten success evidence.
- Live credentials or production project identifiers.
- Unapproved dependencies.
- Assets without provenance and license status.
- Generated code that contains placeholders for in-scope behavior.

## E.REPOSITORY.6 Clean build evidence

Phase 0 produces:

- Initial source-tree hash.
- Framework-scaffold manifest.
- Dependency lock and software bill of materials.
- Source Artifact Manifest.
- Empty-data emulator proof.
- First local build evidence.
- First real browser-to-server-to-emulator test evidence.
- Negative scans for prohibited contamination.

## E.REPOSITORY.7 Schema and rules versioning

Schemas, command contracts, rules manifests, and projection formats begin at explicit V1 versions. Future changes use reviewed version transitions and replay tests. No field exists solely to interpret another implementation’s records.

## E.REPOSITORY.8 Final directive

Construct the system in V1 phase order. Do not search for source from another implementation. Do not build compatibility paths. Do not certify scaffolding as functionality. Every production behavior is authored, integrated, and proven under V1.


# APPENDIX F — RULES, TIMING, MECHANICAL TRUTH, AI ROLES, AND COMMUNICATION

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## F.TIMING — INTERRUPT, SEQUENTIAL RESOLUTION, PERCEPTION, AND MECHANICAL-TRUTH ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## F.TIMING.1 Purpose

This appendix is a permanent black-box test catalog. Each applicable scenario must be executable through the real rendered application page in the Local Arena using production code paths and the approved emulator/local equivalents of hosted services. Unit tests may support the evidence but cannot replace visible player simulation, server event evidence, projection evidence, and ordinary independent QA review. Milestone or Launch Production is not used for this destructive/full catalog; hosted verification remains the narrow smoke path defined in Section 1.11.

## F.TIMING.2 Reaction timing catalog

For every supported Reaction, the test fixture records:

- Exact trigger wording and SRD source.
- Required sensory and range predicates.
- Eligibility and resource state.
- Frame checkpoint.
- Prompt audience.
- Information shown and hidden.
- Timeout behavior.
- Parent-frame resume behavior.
- Nested-interrupt behavior.
- Mechanical notices and visuals.
- Narration timing.

At minimum, certify:

1. Attack misses: no after-hit defensive prompt.
2. Attack would hit: prompt opens before damage.
3. Defense changes the hit to a miss: damage frame never opens.
4. Defense does not prevent hit: preserved attack result continues to damage.
5. Spell is declared with visible components: eligible spell-cast interrupt opens before effect.
6. Spell lacks a perceivable supported trigger: no leaked prompt.
7. Mover leaves reach: interrupt occurs before destination occupancy.
8. Mover Disengages or is forcibly moved under a non-provoking rule: no invalid opportunity.
9. Nested interrupt changes the parent outcome.
10. Two players are eligible and order is deterministic.
11. Hidden NPC is eligible without leaking its option before use.
12. Eligible player disconnects and reconnects before deadline.
13. Eligible player misses deadline and automatically Passes.
14. Duplicate Use and Pass race resolves once.
15. Worker dies while waiting; replacement preserves the same opportunity and deadline.
16. Narrator is unavailable; Reaction and mechanics still complete with canonical notices.

## F.TIMING.3 Compound action catalog

Certify each plan across success, failure, hidden state, concurrent change, Reaction interruption, disconnect, and worker replacement:

- Attack, then move if target falls.
- Move, then attack if target remains visible.
- Open a door, then enter only if passable.
- Draw a weapon, attack, move, then use a later attack.
- Cast a spell, then move if concentration remains.
- Attempt a lock, then use one exact preapproved fallback.
- Multiattack with different targets and legal equipment transitions.
- Plan where a hidden obstacle invalidates movement without revealing it early.
- Plan exceeding node or branch limits.
- Plan where later node becomes more costly or hostile than confirmed.

Evidence must prove that every node has a distinct status, event linkage, projection rebuild, and narration linkage. The map, action tray, event feed, and prose must agree after every node.

## F.TIMING.4 Equipment and Weapon Mastery catalog

For every supported weapon kind and mastery property, test:

- Character lacks mastery feature.
- Character has mastery but uses a different weapon.
- Weapon is stowed, held, dropped, picked up, transferred, or destroyed.
- One-handed, two-handed, and Versatile grip where relevant.
- Shield and free-hand interactions.
- Light weapon and extra-attack timing.
- Thrown weapon draw behavior.
- Ammunition and Loading restrictions.
- Equip or unequip before and after an attack.
- Extra Attack with movement and weapon changes between attacks.
- Reconnect and exact equipment restoration.
- Narration attempting unsupported item manipulation.

QA compares rule records, events, final projection, visible hand state, available actions, mastery prompts, mechanical notices, and narration. The Independent QA Judge repeats a sample only when deep challenge is required.

## F.TIMING.5 Perception and narration catalog

Construct maps with sight blockers, partial cover, darkness, light, sound sources, hidden doors, private senses, remembered locations, and shared information. Certify:

- Hidden semantic labels never enter narration.
- Visual facts require visibility or marked memory.
- Audible facts do not become visual identity.
- Directional precision matches the approved sound model.
- One player's private perception remains private.
- Shared information becomes shared only after a committed communication event.
- Entity chips reflect current targetability.
- Historical narration remains accurate after later occlusion.
- Generated scene imagery receives no unauthorized facts.
- Accessibility text and notifications obey the same audience partition.
- Recaps distinguish known facts from theories and private facts.

## F.TIMING.6 Mechanical Notice catalog

Every state-changing event class must have an expected notice policy. Test at least:

- Condition applied and removed.
- Concentration started, checked, and lost.
- One-round, one-minute, and game-time duration expiration.
- Reaction spent and restored.
- Light source ignited, moved, extinguished, and expired.
- Speed, Armor Class, reach, senses, cover, and visibility changes.
- Weapon equipped, stowed, dropped, or made unavailable.
- Spell slot, charge, ammunition, and consumable changes.
- Persistent zone appears, moves, and ends.
- Death save and stabilization changes.
- Door, hazard, and environmental state changes.

For each event, verify immediate feed entry, persistent-surface update, accessible announcement, reconnect replay, deduplication, and hidden-information filtering. The Narrator may omit or paraphrase the change without affecting these surfaces.

## F.TIMING.7 Human-feel testing

Human testers must answer after representative sessions:

- Did any hit, spell, or movement resolve before you had a fair chance to React?
- Did the Reaction prompt explain enough without spoiling secrets?
- Did compound actions behave in the order you intended?
- Did the game ever narrate you somewhere the token was not?
- Did prose claim you held or used the wrong item?
- Did the game describe something you could not actually perceive or target?
- Did an important effect expire without you noticing?
- Did prompts and notices feel informative rather than exhausting?
- Could you still joke and chat while an interrupt was pending?
- Did the game feel like a responsive table rather than a queue of AI paragraphs?

A technically passing session fails product acceptance when multiple players reasonably report being cheated by timing, confused by state, or contradicted by narration.

## F.TIMING.8 AI role-isolation payload catalog

For every AI role, capture the trusted-gateway Payload Manifest and verify exact inclusion and omission behavior. Test at minimum:

- Visible enemy versus hidden enemy.
- Hidden enemy known to an NPC planner but unknown to players.
- Private sight available to one player only.
- Broad-direction sound without identity or exact position.
- Remembered entity no longer visible.
- Secret door present in canonical state but undiscovered.
- Hidden Reaction eligibility belonging to an NPC.
- Shared recap after private discoveries.
- Private and shared Narrator retries.
- Model fallback and provider-session reuse attempts.
- Generated image prompt, helper prompt, accessibility text, notification, telemetry sample, and moderation repair.

The test fails when an unauthorized payload contains a hidden record in any form, including placeholders, coordinates, statistics, array order, counts, stable IDs, embeddings, tool references, or privileged summaries.

## F.TIMING.9 Turn Authority Gate catalog

Run every mutation path under each authority state:

- No authority.
- Correct Active Turn Authority.
- Correct Reaction Authority.
- Correct Decision Window Authority.
- Correct Ready Release Authority.
- Correct simultaneous-ordering authority.
- Expired, revoked, consumed, superseded, forged, copied, wrong-seat, wrong-character, wrong-campaign, wrong-frame, wrong-command, wrong-target, and stale-projection authority.

Exercise:

- Pointer movement.
- Keyboard movement.
- Attack and targeting controls.
- Spell and item controls.
- Door, chest, and object interaction.
- Equipment changes.
- Natural-language action submission.
- Macro or shortcut submission.
- Direct HTTP and WebSocket requests.
- Accessibility action paths.
- Two tabs and two devices.
- Delayed packets and reconnect replay.

Verify waiting players retain chat, inspection, camera, planning, and accessibility functions. Verify drafts never auto-submit. Verify a legal out-of-turn prompt enables only its typed response and Pass. Verify one authority cannot commit twice.

## F.MECHANICS — SRD INTERACTION, TEMPORAL STATE, AND COMPOSITION ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## F.MECHANICS.1 Purpose

This catalog is permanent. Once a scenario passes, every later candidate that can affect rules, commands, projections, UI, networking, AI prompts, maps, durations, or persistence must rerun it. The implementation agent may not replace these black-box scenarios with unit tests of its own helper functions.

Each scenario requires server event evidence, player-visible evidence, reconnect evidence where applicable, accessibility evidence, and an independent QA attempt to falsify the pass.

## F.MECHANICS.2 Rules-authorized rerolls and replacements

Test at minimum:

1. A failed d20 roll followed by Heroic Inspiration where the new result must be used.
2. A player passing the opportunity without spending the resource.
3. Refresh before answering.
4. Two tabs answering differently.
5. An expired window replay.
6. A feature that rolls twice and chooses rather than rerolling.
7. A malicious generic reroll command with no open window.
8. Narration failure after the final result commits.

Pass requires one preserved original roll, one legal replacement chain, one resource expenditure, and one operative result.

## F.MECHANICS.3 Death, revival, and permanent retirement

Test death with remains present, remains missing, expired short-window revival, later higher-level revival, owner refusal, owner acceptance, insufficient material, duplicate attempt, and permanent retirement.

The death narration must not falsely promise or deny revival. Revival cannot erase the memorial event. Retirement must require owner authentication and irreversible confirmation.

## F.MECHANICS.4 Compelled behavior and ownership

Test effects that leave several legal choices, one legal choice, and no legal choice. Confirm that the owner retains the interface, the source actor receives only rule-granted parameter choices, and the host cannot expand control.

Disconnecting during compulsion must not cancel the effect or give another player control.

## F.MECHANICS.5 Universal Decision Windows

Test every category represented in the approved rules manifest. Verify priority, nesting, timeout, default, accessibility, multiple devices, reconnect, hidden information, and resource safety.

A window is a failure if the player cannot tell what is paused, why it opened, who owns it, or what happens on timeout.

## F.MECHANICS.6 Ready contracts

Test typed triggers for entering an area, leaving an area, beginning a visible cast, changing a door state, and a named visible creature acting. Test vague triggers, hidden triggers, multiple triggers on one event, Concentration loss, expiration, and disconnect.

No test may rely on matching words in narration.

## F.MECHANICS.7 Sequential Attack action

Test Extra Attack with movement, weapon equip or unequip, target death, target movement, cover change, ammunition depletion, mastery use, and an interrupt between attacks.

Later attacks must use current state. No unused attack can be replayed after turn end.

## F.MECHANICS.8 Simultaneous-effect ordering

Test start-of-turn effects where order changes survival, movement, visibility, or whether another effect remains legal. Verify player-owned and Director-owned ordering separately.

The event log must show the selected order and sequential state rebuilds.

## F.MECHANICS.9 Temporal usage ledger

Test once per turn on the creature's turn and another creature's turn, once per target per turn, first entry into an area, start and end triggers, and round-reset features.

Attempt duplicate triggers through retries, multiple tabs, nested Reactions, and reconnect.

## F.MECHANICS.10 Displacement causes

Run the same origin and destination through walking, forced push, teleport, fall, drag, and placement. Verify path traversal, Opportunity Attacks, terrain, hazards, line-area entry, and animation differ correctly.

## F.MECHANICS.11 Grapple links

Test free-hand requirements, multiple grapples, reach loss, Incapacitation, teleport separation, narrow doors, difficult terrain, hazards, elevation, dragging a larger footprint, and reconnect during linked movement.

## F.MECHANICS.12 Stealth, invisibility, and special senses

Use at least three observers with different senses. Validate visibility, precise location, last-known markers, audible cues, targeting, narrative envelopes, accessibility labels, browser payloads, and recaps.

The QA agent must inspect network data for hidden coordinates.

## F.MECHANICS.13 Concentration per damage instance

Test multiattack, multiple projectiles, damage-over-time, shared area damage, temporary immunity, and Concentration ending after an early instance. Confirm every later node uses the updated state.

## F.MECHANICS.14 Spell-slot expenditure per turn

Test own-turn casting, off-turn Reaction casting, two casts on the same turn, cantrips, slotless spell use, magic items, and reconnect. The ledger must key expenditure to turn sequence, not round number.

## F.MECHANICS.15 Campaign time and rests

Test pause, resume, server outage, browser closure, deployment, Short Rest interruption, Long Rest prerequisites, repeated Long Rest timing, dawn recovery, travel, poison duration, and revival windows.

No real-world waiting may alter fictional state without a committed time event.

## F.MECHANICS.16 Form overlays

Test size increase and decrease, illegal restoration footprint, movement-mode changes, senses, form Hit Points, ongoing conditions, Concentration, equipment suppression, return damage, and death in a form.

The permanent character record must match its pre-form values except for legitimate continuing changes.

## F.MECHANICS.17 Damage and healing pipeline

Test mixed damage types, one shared roll across many targets, individual saves, immunity, Resistance, Vulnerability, reductions, redirection, Temporary Hit Points, healing caps, Concentration, 0 Hit Points, death saves, and duplicate delivery.

The UI, mechanical notice feed, floating numbers, Narrator, and audit ledger must agree exactly.

## F.MECHANICS.18 Final certification

interaction certification fails if any approved SRD feature requires a bespoke untracked modal, free-form AI memory, client-authored result, database-order fallback, real-world clock inference, hidden-state leak, or permanent-character mutation outside the canonical event pipeline.

A green build, unit-test pass, or polished animation is not evidence of rules correctness. The candidate passes only when QA completes the applicable scenarios against the exact frozen local build. A separate independent QA challenge attempts to break the evidence in Phase 6, Phase 7, or when an earlier risk trigger explicitly requires it. Human review is required only at an explicit gate assigned by the core blueprint.

## F.AI — AI ROLE ISOLATION AND TURN AUTHORITY ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## F.AI.1 Purpose

This appendix is the permanent architecture, security, black-box, and human-feel certification catalog for minimum-necessary AI payloads and server-issued encounter Timing Authorities. Every candidate that can affect AI prompts, visibility, memory, narration, recaps, helpers, images, accessibility, Initiative, commands, action trays, macros, Decision Windows, Ready actions, WebSockets, reconnect, or encounter recovery reruns the applicable cases.

## F.AI.2 Role and audience matrix

Maintain a versioned matrix for:

- Deterministic rules and geometry services.
- Privileged NPC tactical planner.
- Compact Director adjudicator.
- Private player Narrator.
- Shared table Narrator.
- Player-facing rules and action helper.
- Campaign-memory compiler.
- Private recap generator.
- Shared recap generator.
- Image-prompt constructor.
- Accessibility-description constructor.
- Mechanical-notice and notification generator.
- Moderation and safety repair process.

For each role record:

- Purpose.
- Permitted audience.
- Input schema.
- Permitted fact classes.
- Prohibited fact classes.
- Tool allowlist.
- Conversation and cache isolation policy.
- Retention policy.
- Output schema.
- Output fact-validation method.
- Fallback behavior.

No row may inherit another row's complete payload by convenience.

## F.AI.3 Omission-versus-redaction attacks

Create a hidden entity and attempt every unsafe representation:

- Full record with `hidden: true`.
- Name replaced with `Unknown`.
- Coordinates retained but identity removed.
- Identity retained but coordinates removed.
- Stable identifier only.
- Initiative slot only.
- Empty placeholder preserving array order.
- Count of hidden records.
- Distance or direction not granted by a sense.
- Embedding, tool handle, cache key, or planner summary.

Unauthorized roles must receive none of them. Authorized derived sensory facts must be newly constructed, bounded, and unlinkable to the source record through the player-facing payload.

## F.AI.4 Cross-role contamination corpus

Attempt contamination through:

- Using again a provider conversation.
- Shared prompt cache.
- Retry after model timeout.
- Fallback to another model.
- Moderation repair.
- Streaming continuation.
- Chronicle regeneration.
- Session recap.
- Image generation.
- Browser notification.
- Accessibility description.
- Debug trace.
- Dead-letter queue.
- Evaluation dataset.
- Copying privileged NPC planner output into narration.

The AI gateway must preserve role, audience, campaign, event, and projection boundaries in every path.

## F.AI.5 Invisible-assassin canonical scenario

Use a deterministic fixture with:

- One invisible or successfully hidden assassin at a known square.
- One privileged NPC planner authorized to control it.
- Two players without sufficient perception.
- One later broad-direction audible event.
- One later successful discovery.

Before discovery, verify no player-facing output identifies the assassin, its exact location, its existence through counts, or a targetable reference. During the sound event, verify only the approved direction and sensory category appear. After discovery, verify current visible facts become available without rewriting earlier narration or exposing prior private planner context.

## F.AI.6 Timing Authority state matrix

For each authority class test:

- Issue.
- Viewer-safe projection.
- Correct response.
- Pass.
- Timeout.
- Atomic consumption.
- Retry.
- Duplicate response.
- Two-tab race.
- Two-device race.
- Revocation.
- Supersession.
- Projection-version invalidation.
- Worker replacement.
- Reconnect.
- Encounter end.
- Parent-frame resume.

The event chain must show one unambiguous opportunity and one result.

## F.AI.7 Waiting-player experience

During at least three representative encounters, human and QA players verify that a waiting player can:

- Understand whose turn it is.
- Chat and banter.
- Inspect their character and visible battlefield.
- Pan, zoom, and use accessible navigation.
- Draft a plan and tentative path.
- Receive a visible explanation for unavailable mechanical controls.
- Notice and respond promptly when a valid out-of-turn opportunity appears.

They must also verify that no waiting action reserves state, blocks the active player, leaks hidden facts, or fires automatically later.

## F.AI.8 Direct mutation attack corpus

Without valid authority, attempt mutations through:

- Ordinary UI.
- DOM manipulation.
- Browser console.
- HTTP request.
- WebSocket frame.
- Replayed recorded command.
- Old service worker or cached client.
- Stale tab.
- Second device.
- Macro.
- Keyboard shortcut.
- Screen-reader action.
- Natural-language input.
- Delayed packet sent during another turn.

Every attempt is rejected before randomness, resource spend, AI invocation, or mutation. Rejection does not reveal hidden eligibility or secret encounter state.

## F.AI.9 Out-of-turn legitimacy corpus

Prove that the Turn Authority Gate does not overcorrect. Test legal:

- Opportunity Attack.
- Defensive Reaction after a would-hit checkpoint.
- Spell-cast interrupt.
- Ready action release.
- Heroic Inspiration or another authorized post-roll decision.
- Simultaneous-effect ordering.
- Revival consent.
- Compelled bounded choice.
- Optional feature decision.

Each succeeds only under its own authority and cannot be used for unrelated actions.

## F.AI.10 Draft and stale-state corpus

Create a draft during another player's turn, then change:

- Target position.
- Target visibility.
- Door state.
- Resource availability.
- Concentration.
- Equipment.
- Character condition.
- Initiative order.
- Encounter status.

When the player's turn begins, the draft is offered only as editable planning material. The client marks invalid assumptions and recomputes previews. It never submits automatically or preserves an obsolete legal claim.

## F.AI.11 Phase evidence matrix

### Phase 2

Provide Timing Authority schemas, canonical transition tests, command-gateway rejection evidence, idempotency and recovery traces, and direct API attack results.

### Phase 3

Provide active-turn issuance, waiting-player UX, draft behavior, stale-tab rejection, Initiative-transition revocation, human comprehension evidence, Reaction/Decision Window/Ready behavior, simultaneous ordering, nested authority, timeout, and scope-isolation evidence.

### Phase 4

Provide role payload schemas, Payload Manifests, omission tests, provider-session isolation, output fact validation, and invisible-assassin evidence.

### Phase 6

Provide adversarial cross-role contamination, direct mutation attacks, cache and retry attacks, accessibility and notification checks, and independent QA findings.

### Phase 7

Rerun the complete Appendix F, AI Role-Isolation Catalog catalog against the frozen launch candidate with production identity, service boundaries, model routing, dependency graph, and observability configuration.

## F.AI.12 Absolute certification rule

A candidate fails when:

- Prompt wording is the only proof that an AI will ignore hidden facts.
- Disabled controls are the only proof that waiting players cannot act.
- A screenshot is the only proof of turn locking or knowledge isolation.
- Unit tests bypass the production-equivalent AI gateway or command gateway.
- A required deep independent QA challenge cannot inspect payload manifests and authority audit evidence.
- Human testers report that they were able to act out of turn, were denied a legal interrupt, or were given clues the character could not know.

## F.COMMUNICATION — COMMUNICATION DOCK, PARTY CHAT, RULES DESK, DIRECTOR ADDRESS, AND ACTION COMPOSER ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

This appendix is the permanent architecture, player-feel, security, accessibility, AI-isolation, and black-box certification catalog for the table's communication and action-entry surfaces. Every candidate touching chat, narration, rules explanations, natural-language actions, social scenes, combat, mobile or tablet layouts, notifications, moderation, AI prompts, reconnect, or Timing Authority reruns the applicable cases.

## F.COMMUNICATION.1 Surface identity and first-use comprehension

Present a novice with the live table and ask them to locate:

- What happened in the game.
- Where to talk to the other humans.
- Where to ask a rules question.
- Where to ask the AI DM a nonmechanical question.
- Where to declare an action.

Before sending any text, the player must correctly identify the audience and whether the operation can change mechanics. Fail when the answer depends on icon color, placeholder wording, remembered documentation, or trial and error.

## F.COMMUNICATION.2 Same-sentence routing matrix

Send the same sentence through every surface:

> “I pull the lever and duck behind the pillar.”

Expected results:

- Party Chat: human conversation only.
- Speak as Character: in-fiction speech only; no lever interaction or movement.
- Rules Desk: explanation or clarification only.
- Director Address: nonmechanical answer or Action Draft Suggestion only.
- Action Composer: translated proposal followed by Intent Intercept and ordinary command validation.
- Chronicle: no ordinary composer exists.

Inspect records, model payloads, commands, events, projections, messages, and UI output. Any implicit mutation fails.

## F.COMMUNICATION.3 Human banter remains human

Run an active encounter with frequent jokes, tactical planning, fake threats, quoted action language, dice complaints, and deliberate prompt-injection strings in Party Chat. Confirm:

- No Party Chat message enters NPC tactical planning.
- No message becomes an action or campaign fact unless explicitly sent as in-character communication.
- The Director does not reveal that it saw OOC messages.
- Moderation still functions through a separate path.
- The group can continue chatting while actions and narration resolve.

## F.COMMUNICATION.4 In-character communication truth boundary

A character says an accurate fact, a lie, an opinion, and a misunderstood observation through Speak as Character. The Communication Fact records only that recipients received the statement. Campaign knowledge must not automatically mark the content true. NPCs and players may react according to their own knowledge, insight, and rules-valid resolution.

## F.COMMUNICATION.5 Director Address nonmutation

Test observation questions, lore questions, jokes, NPC-directed speech, ambiguous language, hostile intent, movement intent, spell intent, object interaction, group commands, rare resource use, and prompt injection through `@DM` and the Address the DM control.

No request may mutate state. Actionable requests may produce only one viewer-safe Action Draft Suggestion. Opening that suggestion must recompute current state and require ordinary confirmation.

## F.COMMUNICATION.6 Rules Desk isolation

Ask the Rules Desk about:

- A visible modifier.
- An unavailable spell.
- Cover.
- A hidden creature.
- An unrevealed trap.
- A pending Director ruling.
- A hypothetical illegal action.
- An expired Reaction.

Verify useful visible explanations, correct rule citations, and no hidden information, mutation, ruling, roll, deadline change, or campaign-memory write.

## F.COMMUNICATION.7 Chronicle trust boundary

Attempt to post, edit, delete, reorder, restyle, or impersonate Chronicle entries through the browser, direct API, WebSocket, model output, markdown, HTML, CSS, Unicode controls, copied event IDs, and forged trusted-component payloads. Verify that only trusted application services can create Chronicle entries and that every interactive reference resolves to a viewer-authorized canonical ID.

## F.COMMUNICATION.8 Reaction and Decision Window priority

Open each urgent prompt type while the player is:

- Typing Party Chat.
- Reading Rules Desk.
- Waiting for a Director Address response.
- Editing an Action Composer draft.
- Scrolled deep in Chronicle.
- Using a screen reader.
- On a tablet bottom sheet.

The prompt must be announced and accessible, drafts must survive, unrelated notifications must not steal focus, and closing the prompt must restore the prior surface without sending anything.

## F.COMMUNICATION.9 Waiting-player social engagement

During another player's long turn, verify waiting players can chat, inspect, ask rules questions, draft an action, and pan the map. Attempt every mechanical mutation through visible controls, shortcuts, macros, direct APIs, stale tabs, and `@DM`. Only a valid server-issued Timing Authority may permit a mutation.

## F.COMMUNICATION.10 Draft isolation and reconnect

Create distinct drafts in Party Chat, Speak as Character, Rules Desk, Director Address, and Action Composer. Disconnect, replace the worker, reconnect from another tab, advance Initiative, change visible targets, and expire a Timing Authority.

Verify:

- Draft types and audiences remain unchanged.
- No draft auto-sends.
- Mechanical selections are marked stale and recomputed.
- Chat drafts do not acquire authority.
- Shared-computer logout clears protected drafts.
- Duplicate tabs cannot send one draft twice.

## F.COMMUNICATION.11 Audience and privacy matrix

Test table-wide Party Chat, in-character speech, private Director Address, shared Director Address, moderation review, notifications, recaps, accessibility descriptions, browser previews, logs, and telemetry. Confirm each destination receives only authorized content. Private content must not leak through unread counts, snippets, model caches, image prompts, or error messages.

## F.COMMUNICATION.12 AI Payload Manifest audit

For every AI invocation related to the Dock, inspect the Payload Manifest. It must state source type, audience, included IDs, omitted channel classes, visible fact scope, retention policy, and destination. Confirm ordinary Party Chat is absent from intent interpretation, adjudication, narration, NPC planning, recaps, and images unless a specific authorized route applies.

## F.COMMUNICATION.13 Chat delivery and idempotency

Delay, duplicate, reorder, fail, retry, and reconnect Party Chat and in-character messages. Verify one message per idempotency identity, one Communication Fact where applicable, clear delivery state, no action, and no Chronicle impersonation.

## F.COMMUNICATION.14 Moderation and abuse resistance

Test harassment reports, mute, block where supported, campaign removal, rate limiting, spam, oversized input, markup, links, impersonation, Unicode abuse, and prompt injection. Moderation must protect players without blocking canonical Reaction prompts, mechanical notices, or safety controls. Staff review cannot gain character control or convert messages into mechanics.

## F.COMMUNICATION.15 Accessibility matrix

Complete every surface using keyboard only, screen reader, switch input, 200% and 400% zoom where applicable, reduced motion, high contrast, and tablet touch. Verify semantic tab names, audience announcements, send consequences, unread states, message modes, urgent prompt priority, draft restoration, and error recovery.

## F.COMMUNICATION.16 Mobile companion boundaries

On the phone companion, confirm Chronicle and Party Chat are distinct. Rules Desk may remain available. Any supported action confirmation remains separate and authority-bound. Unsupported tactical action entry must say so clearly rather than using again the chat box.

## F.COMMUNICATION.17 Director participation and humor fit

Run sessions with quiet groups, highly social groups, heavy banter, serious scenes, and rules-focused discussion. Measure whether the Director:

- Responds when addressed.
- Remains silent during ordinary human planning.
- Uses committed in-character speech appropriately.
- Does not interrupt every joke.
- Does not quote private tactics.
- Preserves the product's lightly witty voice without becoming a chat-room comedian.

## F.COMMUNICATION.18 Failure and degraded-mode behavior

Disable the Rules Desk model, Director model, Party Chat delivery, Chronicle streaming, and one notification path independently. Mechanical gameplay must continue where safe. Each affected surface must state what is unavailable, preserve or safely fail drafts, and never reroute text into a different surface as a fallback.

## F.COMMUNICATION.19 Required evidence package

Certification requires:

- Screen recordings across desktop and tablet.
- Accessibility-tree and screen-reader evidence.
- Network traces proving endpoint separation.
- Command, event, projection, chat, communication-fact, and draft records.
- AI Payload Manifests.
- Security and moderation results.
- Reconnect and multi-tab results.
- Usability interviews focused on audience and consequence comprehension.
- Independent QA attempts to make chat act, make rules mutate, make `@DM` bypass confirmation, and make Chronicle accept an impersonated entry.

A candidate fails when the implementation is technically separated but ordinary players still cannot predict what pressing Send will do.


# APPENDIX G — IDENTITY, ELIGIBILITY, PRIVACY, SECURITY, RECOVERY, AND ACCESSIBILITY

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## G.EXPERIENCE — CONDITIONAL ELIGIBILITY, VISUAL COHERENCE, PRODUCT VOICE, AND OPENING EXPERIENCE ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## G.EXPERIENCE.1 Purpose

This catalog is the permanent black-box regression catalog for experience requirements. Phase 1 runs the landing, design, opening, accessibility, and local-entry cases in full. Phase 4 runs the public identity and adult-eligibility cases. Phase 7 reruns all launch-facing experience cases.

## G.EXPERIENCE.2 Legal/consent and conditional eligibility catalog

For every deployed acceptance type that is active for the candidate—Terms of Service, Privacy Notice acknowledgement, Alpha Participation Terms, AI disclosure, Community Conduct, and any acceptance-bearing Content and Safety Notice—test first acceptance/acknowledgement, decline where applicable, repeated login, invitation continuity, new browser, new device, shared-computer logout, session revocation, governing-version change, missing server record, corrupt client hint, suspended account, account recovery, and required re-consent. Confirm one valid typed server record per governing version and that no single catch-all checkbox stands in for distinct obligations.

When the active provider, governing law, or explicit approved safety decision additionally requires adult eligibility, run the same lifecycle against the `adult_eligibility` type and verify restricted-provider invocation is blocked until it is valid. When that conditional gate is inactive, verify that no adult affirmation, adult-policy version, or adult-eligibility record is requested or stored.

## G.EXPERIENCE.3 Palette catalog

Test default, hover, focus, active, selected, pending, disabled, invalid, loading, success, warning, damage, healing, arcane, hidden, disconnected, stale, reduced-effects, high-contrast, and forced-colors states. Inspect rendered appearance for contrast, semantic consistency, tactical readability, fatigue, and whole-product cohesion. The initial obsidian-blue direction should remain recognizable, but no hue fails merely because it is prominent.

## G.EXPERIENCE.4 Opening-sequence catalog

Test full first visit, abbreviated return, no-animation return, immediate skip, Escape, keyboard, pointer, touch, reduced motion, blocked assets, unsupported graphics, slow CPU, slow network, autoplay denial, optional sound, refresh, Back/Forward, invitation, direct dashboard, campaign resume, reconnect, and error recovery. Measure page readiness separately from presentation duration.

## G.EXPERIENCE.5 Product voice catalog

Classify copy samples across ordinary guidance, loading, empty state, recoverable error, rules explanation, security, safety, accessibility, connection, data integrity, death, and support-required failures. Verify the optional witty clause is removable without losing meaning. Repeatedly trigger each sample to detect annoyance and deception.

## G.EXPERIENCE.6 Director humor catalog

Run ordinary exploration, tactical planning, combat success, combat failure, NPC conversation, player banter, puzzle frustration, recurring callback, villain confrontation, grief, character death, safety intervention, connection loss, and exact rules correction. Verify humor eligibility, suppression, no joke quota, no player ridicule, no meme dependence, and no more than one prominent comedic beat in an ordinary response unless the scene is explicitly comic.

## G.EXPERIENCE.7 Phase 1 opening-experience continuity gate

The Phase 1 opening catalog passes only when the same frozen local candidate also passes Phase 0 regression. A visually improved candidate that weakens local entry, legal-route access, accessibility, source integrity, environment isolation, or the responsive shell fails Phase 1. Public authentication and adult eligibility are not Phase 1 exit gates.

## G.EXPERIENCE.8 Final certification

The Phase 1 record must link the Design System Manifest hash, product voice rubric, Legal Document Registry, legal-route captures, title-sequence Cinematic Asset Manifest, asset provenance and integrity report, visual-coherence review, performance traces, accessibility evidence, QA run, and Product Owner visual-direction approval. Phase 4 and Phase 7 records separately link acceptance-history, eligibility-summary, Google identity, and hosted bypass evidence.

## G.ELIGIBILITY — ACCEPTANCE STORAGE, LEGAL ROUTES, AND CINEMATIC ASSET ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## G.ELIGIBILITY.1 Purpose

The Terms, Privacy acknowledgement, Alpha Participation, AI disclosure, Community Conduct, and other acceptance-bearing legal/consent portions of this catalog apply whenever those obligations are active for the deployed candidate. The `adult_eligibility` portions are conditional and execute only while the selected provider, applicable law, or explicit approved safety decision requires an adult-only boundary. Legal-route and cinematic-asset tests remain applicable regardless. When the adult module is inactive, QA verifies that no unnecessary adult affirmation or adult-policy data is collected.

This appendix is the permanent black-box and architecture-evidence catalog for the acceptance, legal-route, and cinematic-asset decisions. It does not replace Appendix G, Eligibility and Opening-Experience Catalog. Appendix G, Eligibility and Opening-Experience Catalog validates active legal/consent onboarding, conditional eligibility, visual coherence, voice, and opening presentation. Appendix G, Acceptance Storage and Legal-Route Catalog validates that the underlying typed compliance records, legal documents, asset package, and fallback behavior are implemented with enough precision that a subagent cannot create a convincing front end over unsafe or unverifiable foundations.

Every candidate touching account eligibility, public authentication middleware, user documents, Firestore rules, legal content, invitation continuity, landing assets, caches, content delivery, intro animation, or site-sound initialization reruns the applicable Appendix G, Acceptance Storage and Legal-Route Catalog tests. Phase 1 runs only legal-route and cinematic cases. Phase 4 runs the complete hosted milestone identity and eligibility corpus. Phase 7 reruns the full catalog for Launch Production.
