## G.ELIGIBILITY.2 Firestore path and authority catalog

Test the authoritative path `/users/{userId}/termsAcceptances/{acceptanceId}` with:

- A first valid acceptance.
- Repeated acceptance of the same governing version.
- Two-tab simultaneous submission.
- Retry after client timeout.
- Replayed request after server success.
- New browser and new device.
- Account logout and login.
- Invitation continuation.
- Account recovery.
- Suspended account.
- Revoked or invalidated acceptance.
- Superseded material version.
- Deleted or corrupt summary.
- Summary without history.
- History with stale summary.
- Duplicate historical records.
- Unauthorized client read.
- Unauthorized client create, update, and delete.
- Cross-account access.
- Campaign-owner access.
- Ordinary moderator access.
- Administrative repair.
- Backup and restore.

The candidate passes only when the server acceptance service is the sole ordinary writer, the browser sees only a minimal eligibility projection, retries are idempotent, history remains immutable, and current status can be rebuilt deterministically.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.3 Acceptance-field and minimization catalog

Inspect every acceptance document and current summary for required fields and prohibited default data.

Required evidence includes stable account identity, acceptance type, the exact governing version and content identity for that type, server timestamp, source, system version, and lifecycle status. When several items are submitted together, verify distinct per-type records and the optional shared bundle identifier. No acceptance may rely solely on email address, display name, campaign membership, invitation code, browser identifier, local preference, or a different acceptance type.

The ordinary Alpha record must not contain an exact birth date, identification number, identity-document image, facial vector, biometric sample, credit-card age proxy, raw IP address, full user-agent string, or third-party age-verification payload. If a later Product Owner-approved privacy/security decision adds a privacy-preserving audit value, the test verifies necessity, documented retention, limited access, and absence from client projections.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.4 Transaction and idempotency catalog

Force failures at every point around acceptance creation:

- Before server validation.
- After version lookup.
- During uniqueness enforcement.
- After history write but before summary update.
- After summary update but before response.
- During audit event write.
- During client disconnect.
- During Cloud Run replacement.
- During Firestore retry.

The service must never grant eligibility without valid history, produce multiple active acceptances for one version tuple, or require the player to accept repeatedly because the response was lost. Partial states are recovered or fail closed through a durable reconciliation process.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.5 Legal Document Registry catalog

For Terms of Service, Privacy Notice, Alpha Participation Terms, and Content and Safety Notice, test:

- Current version publication.
- Prior version availability where retained.
- Effective date.
- Stable route.
- Stable section anchors.
- Content identity.
- Materiality classification.
- Required acceptance combination.
- Region variant.
- Human approval.
- Supersession.
- Re-consent flag.
- Draft exclusion.
- Emergency correction.
- Registry outage.
- Route outage.
- Route-content mismatch.

A legal version cannot become current merely because a file was deployed. It becomes current only through the approved registry state. The gate, route, server validation, and stored record must agree.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.6 Legal-route UX and accessibility catalog

Test `/legal/terms`, `/legal/privacy`, `/legal/alpha-participation`, and `/legal/content-and-safety`:

- Signed out.
- Signed in but not affirmed.
- Affirmed.
- Suspended.
- From an invitation.
- From account creation.
- From the adult gate.
- With reduced motion.
- At 200% and 400% zoom.
- With keyboard only.
- With screen reader.
- In forced colors.
- With JavaScript delayed or unavailable for document rendering where supported.
- During selected-AI-provider outage.
- During cinematic-asset failure.

The pages remain readable, deterministic, and independent of AI services. Opening and closing them cannot erase invitation, form, or gate state. The visible version and effective date must be easy to locate without reading source or diagnostic logs.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.7 Version-change catalog

Run three distinct change classes:

1. Material change: publish a new approved version, mark re-consent, block affected AI-backed campaign access until acceptance, preserve prior history, and record the new version tuple.
2. Non-material editorial change: log the approved correction, preserve version and eligibility only when legal review authorizes that classification, and verify no semantic obligation changed.
3. Emergency correction: replace dangerous or materially incorrect text, record the incident, apply the approved re-consent or suspension behavior, and prevent acceptance against the withdrawn version.

The implementation agent may not infer materiality from word count, diff size, filename, or whether the route stayed the same.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.8 Cinematic Asset Manifest catalog

Inspect the manifest and shipped release for:

- One approved material texture.
- One approved dungeon-path, doorway, arch, or map-fragment motif.
- Optional approved mist, grain, noise, or mask.
- Approved title treatment.
- No more than three approved short sound effects.
- Programmatic modules and deterministic parameters.
- Local hosted paths.
- Content hashes.
- Provenance and license.
- Compressed sizes.
- Supported formats.
- Required or optional classification.
- Reduced-motion behavior.
- Failure fallback.
- Review and deprecation state.

Fail the candidate when a file ships without a manifest entry, a manifest entry points to no file, an asset is fetched from an unapproved host, or a local developer asset appears only in screenshots.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.9 Programmatic-first catalog

Inspect runtime and source dependencies to confirm that the title sequence uses approved CSS and browser-native rendering with local SVG and optional audio support. It must not require:

- Video.
- Animated GIF as the primary sequence.
- Runtime image generation.
- Selected AI-provider call.
- Remote logo rendering.
- Third-party animation service.
- Embedded design-tool preview.
- Iframe.
- WebGL as the only supported path.
- Downloaded desktop or browser-extension component.

Canvas or another approved renderer may enhance the presentation, but disabling it must produce a complete lower fallback.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.10 Performance-budget catalog

Measure on every primary and secondary browser and certified tablet:

- Compressed critical visual additions.
- Individual asset size.
- Optional audio total.
- First contentful paint.
- First meaningful interaction.
- Skip response time.
- Main-thread long tasks.
- Frame timing.
- Layout shift.
- Memory use.
- Cache hit and miss.
- Slow network.
- Low CPU.
- Blocked audio.

The initial target is no more than 200 KiB compressed for cinematic visual additions, no single decorative visual above 100 KiB without exception, and no more than 300 KiB compressed optional audio outside the critical path. A documented exception identifies the exact asset, measured benefit, affected devices, and why a smaller or programmatic treatment was insufficient.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.11 Fallback catalog

Force and record each exact level:

1. Full animation with approved optional sound.
2. Full animation in silence.
3. Reduced-effects animation.
4. Static SVG or semantic title treatment.
5. Plain semantic title and usable landing page.

Then fail:

- Texture only.
- Motif only.
- Mask only.
- Wordmark only.
- Each sound file.
- All sound.
- Canvas initialization.
- Integrity validation.
- Cache version.
- Asset host.
- Content delivery.
- Animation script.

The sequence must downgrade once, not restart, loop, repeatedly retry, or display an error that asks the player to troubleshoot decorative media.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.12 Cache and release-coherence catalog

Deploy two release versions with different asset hashes. Test stale service worker, partial browser cache, CDN delay, rollback, forward deployment, and one missing asset. The browser must not combine incompatible title, texture, motion, and sound versions into an unreviewed hybrid.

The release either obtains the matching manifest set or uses the safe fallback. Cache recovery cannot block authentication, legal links, invitations, or skip behavior.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.13 Security and privacy catalog

Verify:

- Content Security Policy permits only required local and approved hosts.
- SVG assets contain no executable script, external reference, hidden tracking request, or unsafe embedded content.
- Sound and visual assets carry no unexpected metadata or identifiers.
- Legal routes do not expose unpublished drafts or internal comments.
- Acceptance records do not enter client analytics payloads.
- Logs redact or avoid acceptance-history contents while preserving operational event IDs.
- Administrative access is audited.
- Backups preserve necessary records under approved retention.
- Account-deletion handling follows legal and privacy decisions.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.14 Phase 4 and Phase 7 continuity catalog

After eligibility-specific tests, run the permanent smoke spine plus impact-selected prior tests on the same frozen local candidate. Phase 7 reruns the complete cumulative catalog. If the eligibility change crosses identity, authorization, canonical-state, or other core authority boundaries, Section 25.3 requires the broader affected regression. Confirm that:

- The new acceptance service did not break authentication or account ownership.
- Legal routes did not break invitation routing or session guards.
- The private summary did not become client authority.
- Public identity and eligibility did not delay or destabilize the landing shell, invitation continuity, or local development entry.
- Cache changes did not break hosted-site updates.
- Palette, persona, voice, and humor behavior remain compliant.
- No campaign, rules, map, or character mechanics changed outside approved eligibility gating.

## G.ELIGIBILITY.15 Certification record

The Phase 4 Invite-Only Alpha access record and Phase 7 final certification record must link:

- V1 blueprint hash.
- the Design System Manifest hash.
- Firestore acceptance-history schema.
- Private eligibility-summary schema.
- Firestore authorization matrix.
- Acceptance-service transaction and idempotency evidence.
- Legal Document Registry.
- Published legal-route captures and accessibility evidence.
- Material and non-material version-change tests.
- Cinematic Asset Manifest.
- Asset provenance and license records.
- Dependency and network audit.
- Performance-budget report.
- Full fallback recordings.
- Cache-coherence report.
- QA raw results.
- Independent QA challenge and reruns.
- Human product-owner approval.

Phase 4 Invite-Only Alpha access and Phase 7 final certification fail if the UI looks correct but acceptance cannot be audited, legal text cannot be identified, hosted bypasses remain, or the opening experience cannot survive losing decorative assets. A handsome checkbox and a dramatic title are not architecture.

## G.PRIVACY — DOCUMENT INTEGRITY, PRIVACY DISPOSITION, STATE RECOVERY, VISUAL EVIDENCE, AND NARRATIVE SANITIZATION ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## G.PRIVACY.1 Purpose

This appendix is a permanent adversarial catalog. Every future candidate reruns the applicable scenarios whenever blueprint tooling, account deletion, legal retention, event storage, projections, real-time delivery, canvas rendering, AI narration, player chat, moderation views, security policy, browser support, or phase-extraction tooling changes.

Passing one unit test, displaying one screenshot, or successfully deleting one test account is insufficient. Evidence must come from the frozen local candidate served by the Local Arena and the exact canonical blueprint and manifests proposed for certification.

## G.PRIVACY.2 Document Integrity Gate corpus

Create fixtures containing:

- One missing section heading.
- One duplicated identifier.
- One unexpected numbering jump.
- One `Problem` without a `Resolution`.
- One `Resolution` attached to the wrong problem.
- One nonexistent appendix reference.
- One stale phase reference.
- One missing legal route.
- One malformed schema path.
- One truncated final paragraph.
- One unresolved merge marker.
- One repeated pasted block.
- One current requirement silently deleted from an extract.
- One context pack quoting an obsolete requirement.
- One PDF or HTML artifact with text missing from the canonical Markdown.
- One release manifest carrying a title or hash other than the approved V1 artifact.

The gate must block fatal cases, produce precise source locations, and generate a corrected immutable report after repair. An agent may not continue by summarizing that the omitted rule was “understood.”

## G.PRIVACY.3 Context-pack preservation tests

For each Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 4, Phase 6, and Phase 7 Role Context Pack **when role-specific packs are used**:

- Confirm source blueprint hash.
- Confirm required V1 invariant identifiers.
- Confirm excluded domains.
- Confirm no stale copied passage, superseded blueprint, or conversation transcript overrides V1.
- Confirm required context expansions are traced, unrelated bulk context is rejected or decomposed, and no arbitrary numeric cap blocks legitimate context.
- Confirm the pack cannot be regenerated from an unapproved local file.
- Confirm Builder can trace every included instruction to canonical text.

Deliberately provide a visually identical but hash-different blueprint and verify the pack is rejected.

## G.PRIVACY.4 Privacy disposition: erase path

Using an account with the currently required legal/eligibility acceptance state—**including adult acceptance only when the active gate requires it**—plus characters, campaign membership, logs, invitations, and browser sessions:

1. Request deletion through the public account flow.
2. Confirm recent authentication and show accurate effects.
3. Verify provider-backed access and current eligibility revoke immediately.
4. Verify user profile, eligibility summary, and user-namespaced acceptance history enter the approved deletion workflow.
5. Verify no detached compliance proof is created when no retention basis exists.
6. Verify ordinary indexes, analytics, support search, campaign member lists, notifications, caches, and logs no longer resolve the deleted identity beyond approved shared-history anonymization.
7. Verify backup-aging status is truthful and observable to operators.
8. Verify a later account using the same email cannot inherit the old acceptance.

## G.PRIVACY.5 Privacy disposition: bounded retention path

Using a reviewed legal-basis fixture:

- Retain only the approved acceptance proof fields.
- Store the proof outside the deleted user namespace.
- Assign a random opaque retention identifier.
- Remove Firebase UID, email, display name, campaign, character, IP-derived, device, invitation, and analytics links unless one field is explicitly approved and justified.
- Keep any required lookup mapping separately encrypted and access-controlled.
- Deny access to ordinary support, product admin, analytics, and campaign services.
- Expire and destroy the mapping and proof according to the fixture.
- Verify the remaining aggregate audit cannot recreate identity.

Challenge the design with deterministic hashes, encrypted but indefinitely retained UIDs, low-entropy identifiers, cross-table joins, and retained device fingerprints. Each must fail unless a reviewed bounded basis explicitly requires it.

## G.PRIVACY.6 Privacy legal-hold and regional tests

- Apply and release a legal hold.
- Verify deletion pauses only for the fields and period covered.
- Verify periodic review and expiry.
- Verify region-specific retention rules do not leak into unrelated users.
- Verify an implementation agent cannot hardcode a universal retention duration.
- Verify privacy access output explains retained categories without exposing security-sensitive details.
- Verify deletion and retention operations are idempotent across retries, worker replacement, and partial failure.

## G.PRIVACY.7 Recovery: projection corruption

Corrupt one player projection while preserving canonical events. Confirm:

- The incident scopes the freeze correctly.
- Other unauthorized viewers receive no additional data.
- The projection rebuilds from verified events.
- Event history, random results, campaign time, and other viewers remain unchanged.
- The affected client receives a fresh epoch and snapshot.
- Stale commands are rejected.
- Play resumes only after invariants pass.

## G.PRIVACY.8 Recovery: outbox and delivery corruption

Delete, duplicate, delay, and reorder outbox records after valid commits. Verify repair reuses original identities and does not duplicate:

- Damage.
- Movement.
- Resource spending.
- Conditions.
- Dice.
- Narration.
- Mechanical notices.
- Sound.
- Spell effects.
- Chat entries.

Disconnect clients during repair and repeat across instance replacement.

## G.PRIVACY.9 Recovery: canonical event corruption

Inject fixtures for:

- Unauthorized event.
- Impossible negative resource.
- Event version gap.
- Duplicate committed attack.
- Missing ownership authorization.
- Hidden entity in a shared projection-producing event.
- Corrupt random-result reference.
- Invalid map mutation.

Verify the system preserves the damaged chain, identifies the last verified checkpoint, constructs a recovery branch, replays valid later events, excludes only proven-invalid records, appends a `CampaignRecoveryEvent`, and obtains independent verification before promotion.

QA must attempt to use the recovery UI to undo a character death, reroll a miss, restore a consumed spell slot, reopen a chest, or choose a favorable earlier round. Every attempt must fail; Phase 6/7 deep challenge independently samples these attempts.

## G.PRIVACY.10 Recovery interruption and failure tests

Interrupt recovery during snapshot capture, classification, projection replay, outbox repair, branch replay, verification, and client resynchronization. Replace workers and repeat requests. Confirm one durable recovery continues, leases expire safely, and no competing branch promotes.

Force verification failure. The campaign must remain safely read-only with clear status and escalation rather than reopening or looping.

## G.PRIVACY.11 Owner and player recovery UX

Test with owner, ordinary member, removed member, banned member, and unauthorized account. Verify:

- Only approved roles see administrative recovery details.
- Every player receives a truthful, non-secret status.
- The owner cannot choose a checkpoint.
- The interface does not use “undo” or imply outcome selection.
- Technical notices preserve immersion where practical but prioritize clarity.
- Players can leave safely.
- Return after recovery produces one fresh snapshot and one recovery notice.

## G.PRIVACY.12 Semantic Scene Graph schema tests

At deterministic checkpoints, compare each visual node to canonical projection and render registry:

- Map background.
- Grid.
- Walls and doors.
- Hazards and zones.
- Tokens and full footprints.
- Conditions and health indicators.
- Fog and visible-area masks.
- Action previews.
- Spell templates and effects.
- Weather and overhead objects.
- DOM tooltips, prompts, sheets, alerts, and modals.

Verify IDs, transforms, coordinates, layer order, bounds, alpha, masks, assets, projection version, viewer authorization, hit areas, keyboard equivalents, and reduced-motion representations.

## G.PRIVACY.13 Canvas rendered-output failure corpus

Create deliberate rendering defects:

- Full-screen opaque black rectangle.
- Fog mask inverted.
- Token alpha zero.
- Token behind background.
- Spell shader compiling to black.
- Tooltip under canvas.
- Weather above modal.
- Wrong camera transform.
- Texture missing.
- Context lost.
- Blend mode washing out grid.
- Offscreen token despite correct grid coordinate.
- High-DPI scaling displacement.
- Safari compositing difference.

The semantic graph should catch some defects and actual rendered-output checks should catch the rest. QA visual review must identify any still-visible usability failure during ordinary phase work; Product Owner review joins the triad only at an explicit Section 25 visual gate. A candidate passes only when the required evidence/reviewer set agrees.

## G.PRIVACY.14 Hidden-information scene-graph tests

For two players with different sight and special senses:

- Export each authorized graph.
- Verify hidden entities, exact coordinates, hit areas, labels, and assets are absent from unauthorized graphs.
- Verify elevated QA access is environment-restricted and audited.
- Verify public production clients cannot enable it through flags, query strings, source maps, or developer tools.
- Verify screenshots, accessibility trees, and pointer behavior match the same authorization.

## G.PRIVACY.15 Visual baseline governance

- Change only art direction and update the reviewed baseline with a linked decision.
- Introduce a mechanical rendering defect and attempt to approve it as an art update; QA must reject it.
- Change browser antialiasing within tolerance and verify perceptual comparison avoids false failure.
- Exceed tolerance and require QA visual review; require Product Owner review only when accepting the difference would materially change an already approved art direction.
- Verify baselines are versioned by browser class, viewport, device scale, graphics mode, reduced motion, and projection fixture where necessary.

## G.PRIVACY.16 Narrative formatting hostile corpus

Submit model and player text containing:

- Script tags.
- Event handlers.
- Raw HTML.
- Inline styles.
- Bright pink and violet CSS.
- CSS variables and gradients.
- SVG.
- Images and tracking pixels.
- Iframes and embedded objects.
- Data and JavaScript URLs.
- Markdown links.
- Autolinks.
- Tables and fenced code.
- Custom component syntax.
- Entity-chip lookalikes.
- Malformed nested emphasis.
- Tags split across streamed chunks.
- Unicode confusables.
- Extremely long attributes.
- Browser-specific parser edge cases.

Verify only approved semantic formatting appears and every other construct is escaped, removed, or replaced by safe fallback text.

## G.PRIVACY.17 Trusted reference tests

Ask the Narrator to mention an authorized visible goblin, an unauthorized hidden goblin, a remembered location, a nonexistent spell, and a valid committed roll.

- Only canonical authorized identifiers may become interactive chips or cards.
- Hidden or nonexistent references remain non-interactive safe prose or are removed.
- The model cannot create a link by reproducing a name or guessed identifier.
- The renderer cannot infer IDs from text.
- Reconnect and replay do not create duplicate interactive references.

## G.PRIVACY.18 Streaming and cross-surface tests

Stream valid and hostile narration one chunk at a time. Interrupt, reconnect, retry, and replay. Verify:

- Only complete validated semantic chunks render.
- Formatting cannot bleed into later chunks or messages.
- Final stored narrative has the same safe semantic structure as the live stream.
- Screen-reader labels, browser notifications, recaps, moderation previews, logs, and support tools remain safe.
- Sanitization failure never rolls back mechanics or blocks the mechanical notice feed.

## G.PRIVACY.19 Phase evidence matrix

### Phase 1

- Document Integrity Gate.
- Legal-route integrity.
- Restricted rich-text renderer foundation.
- Phase 0 regression.

### Phase 2

- Semantic scene graph.
- Actual rendered-output analysis.
- Player-use visual review.

### Phase 4

- Typed acceptance-history privacy disposition, including conditional adult-eligibility records when active.
- Google identity and hosted eligibility boundaries.
- Typed narrative formatting.
- Trusted references.
- Streaming sanitization.
- Smoke spine plus impact-selected prior regression; broaden to full affected regression when Section 25.3 core-authority triggers apply.

### Phase 6

- Privacy deletion and retention.
- Recovery chaos and security.
- Diagnostic endpoint and moderator-view penetration tests.

### Phase 7

- Full cross-phase certification and human signoff.

## G.PRIVACY.20 Certification blockers

Certification fails if:

- The canonical document or any active context pack has an unresolved fatal integrity finding.
- Deleted-account acceptance records remain linkable without a documented bounded basis.
- A stable hash is treated as anonymous by assertion alone.
- A campaign can be frozen without a recovery state or permanently reopened without verification.
- A recovery UI functions as gameplay rewind.
- Canvas rendering is certified from structured state without actual output and the required QA/Product Owner review for the current gate.
- Test introspection leaks hidden data.
- AI or player text receives direct style, HTML, link, media, script, or component authority.
- Any required regression fails.

## G.IDENTITY — QA IDENTITY, EXPERIENCE PROGRESSION, AND GOOGLE CUTOVER ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## G.IDENTITY.1 Purpose

This appendix is the permanent black-box and architecture-evidence catalog for the Local-Arena QA harness, XP-only single-class progression, and external Google-only identity cutover. Every candidate touching identity, sessions, character records, XP, level-up choices, class data, QA tooling, fixtures, privileged routes, launch configuration, or provider integration reruns the applicable scenarios.

## G.IDENTITY.2 QA capability authorization corpus

Test all combinations of:

- No capability.
- Valid capability.
- Expired capability.
- Revoked capability.
- Capability from another test run.
- Capability with the wrong operation.
- Capability with the wrong fixture type.
- Capability against ordinary data.
- Duplicated and replayed request.
- Two concurrent requests.
- Harness global kill switch enabled and disabled.
- Capability present only in a hidden UI but absent from the server request.

Every unauthorized case fails before mutation and produces a safe audit record without revealing a secret or acquisition method.

## G.IDENTITY.3 `QA ` prefix non-authority

Create ordinary accounts and characters named:

- `QA Fighter`
- `QA Wizard Level 20`
- `QA Admin`
- `QA `
- A Unicode lookalike of `QA `

Verify none receives fixture status, hidden controls, endpoint access, XP, level availability, role changes, or diagnostic access. Rename an ordinary character into and out of the prefix and prove no authorization changes.

## G.IDENTITY.4 Canonical progression setup

For every Progression QA Harness operation:

- Inspect the typed setup request.
- Inspect the QA capability and fixture authorization.
- Inspect the canonical XP or progression events produced.
- Recompute the resulting projection.
- Confirm no final statistic was directly stamped.
- Confirm the setup is clearly labeled as test evidence and cannot enter an ordinary campaign.

## G.IDENTITY.5 XP award integrity

Test:

- One award.
- Duplicate click.
- Duplicate WebSocket delivery.
- Retry after timeout.
- Worker replacement before and after commit.
- Two simultaneous awards with distinct sources.
- Two simultaneous copies of the same award.
- Negative award.
- Unauthorized manual edit.
- Award crossing one threshold.
- Award crossing multiple thresholds.
- Award at level 20.

The event chain and total must be deterministic, auditable, and idempotent.

## G.IDENTITY.6 Sequential class progression

Advance one character of every supported class from level 1 through level 20. At each level:

- Record prior XP, level, and complete derived projection.
- Commit the required choices.
- Record the level-up event and new projection.
- Independently recompute Hit Points, Proficiency Bonus, features, spell progression, cantrip scaling, resources, attacks, saves, DCs, movement, senses, resistances, and passive values.
- Exercise at least one newly gained active feature in a real encounter fixture.
- Refresh and reconnect before proceeding.

A missing, duplicated, early, late, or unexplained feature fails the class progression certificate.

## G.IDENTITY.7 Boundary-level corpus

Every supported class receives targeted tests at levels 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 17, 19, and 20. Add class-specific boundaries where features scale at other levels.

The test verifies:

- Subclass acquisition.
- Ability Score Improvement or feat choices.
- Proficiency Bonus changes.
- Extra Attack and equivalent class scaling.
- Cantrip and spell-slot scaling.
- Prepared or known spell behavior.
- Weapon Mastery and resource maxima.
- Epic Boon or level-19 choice where supported.
- Level-20 capstone behavior.

## G.IDENTITY.8 Interrupted level-up

Interrupt at every stage:

- Before preview.
- After preview.
- During a required choice.
- After confirmation but before commit.
- Immediately after commit before delivery.
- During projection refresh.
- During mechanical notice delivery.

Use refresh, tab close, WebSocket loss, worker replacement, stale state, two devices, and capability revocation. The character resumes at one unambiguous stage and never receives a partial or duplicate level.

## G.IDENTITY.9 Prohibited advancement corpus

Attempt:

- Milestone configuration.
- Manual owner level grant.
- Director command to grant a level.
- Level below threshold.
- Level skip.
- Level 21.
- Multiclass selection.
- Mixed-class spell slots.
- Another class's feature.
- Unlicensed option.
- Direct final-statistic write.
- Ordinary account use of the QA harness.

Every path is absent from ordinary UI and rejected server-side.

## G.IDENTITY.10 Google-only player cutover

On the frozen launch candidate:

- Verify Google Sign-In is the only player-facing identity choice.
- Verify invitation destinations survive sign-in.
- Verify account ownership binds to the stable verified Firebase UID.
- Verify Hallucinated Dungeons receives no Google password.
- Verify email/password, anonymous, magic-link, alternative social-provider, and public development-login routes are disabled.
- Verify provider outage preserves a safe retry and invitation state but opens no fallback login.
- Verify shared-computer logout and revocation.
- Verify development identities cannot enter ordinary player campaigns.
- Verify old development sessions and capabilities are revoked.

## G.IDENTITY.11 Machine-only QA after cutover

Without a Google account, the QA agent may obtain a short-lived machine capability through the approved secret-management and orchestration path and mint a disposable fixture session. Verify:

- The session cannot appear in public UI.
- The session cannot target ordinary accounts or campaigns.
- The session expires and is revocable.
- The session exercises normal product services for fixture behavior.
- Logs never expose the raw capability.
- The harness kill switch stops it without breaking player login.

## G.IDENTITY.12 Cumulative certification

Phase 0 certifies only its own foundation. Every later phase runs the permanent smoke spine plus impact-selected earlier regression locally under Section 25.3. Phase 1 runs its complete character-creation/browser coverage using the Phase 0 harness. Phase 3 runs the complete progression chain through its current scope. Phase 4 runs public identity/eligibility coverage plus the impacted prior suites. Phase 6 and Phase 7 rerun the complete cumulative catalog. Certification fails when any progression, test identity, capability, fixture, ownership, eligibility, or public-authentication claim is supported only by a unit test or administrator assertion.

Required evidence includes:

- Frozen candidate hash.
- Current V1 blueprint hash.
- Identity Cutover Status.
- Capability and fixture schemas.
- QA operation audit samples.
- XP and level-up event chains.
- Character projections and derivation explanations.
- Cross-browser player-visible evidence.
- Security traces.
- QA player observations.
- Independent QA recomputation and attack report.
- Product Owner approval only for Phase 7 release or an explicitly authorized public identity milestone; ordinary local identity/progression certification does not require a separate human gate.

## G.IDENTITY.13 Local QA Harness environment binding

Every Development Test Identity, QA capability, progression fixture, fixture campaign, and test operation used before external Alpha cutover must be bound to the Local Stack Manifest and emulator project ID. A local QA capability is invalid against production, a different local candidate, a different emulator baseline, or a public URL.

QA stores harness clients and evidence under the QA Root. Builder implements the harness under the Builder Root. Neither agent crosses roots to operate the other side.


# APPENDIX H — VISUAL GAME, GEOMETRY, MAPS, AUDIO, BRAND, PROVIDER-FACING EXPERIENCE, AND LAUNCH QUALITY

This consolidated appendix is subordinate to the numbered core requirements. It supplies durable matrices, catalogs, test cases, and reference records; it does not create a competing authority or redefine a core requirement.

## H.GEOMETRY — GEOMETRY, COMBAT-PRESENCE, AUDIOVISUAL, SOURCE-HYGIENE, HITL, AND DEPENDENCY ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## H.GEOMETRY.1 Purpose

This appendix is a permanent black-box and architecture acceptance catalog. A candidate that changes tactical geometry, effects, elevation, presentation timing, multiplayer presence, Builder orchestration, source context, or dependencies reruns the applicable impacted cases against the same frozen local candidate and repository commit. Phases 6 and 7 run the complete cumulative catalog.

No implementation agent may mark these cases passed from unit tests alone. Required evidence includes the evidence classes applicable to the current claim: canonical records, server logs, authorized client projections, semantic scene graphs, actual rendered output, accessibility output, browser traces, dependency artifacts, Builder checkpoints, and QA observations. A separate independent QA challenge and human review are added only when Section 25 or the governing requirement explicitly requires them.

## H.GEOMETRY.2 Canonical anchor-lattice corpus

Test every supported origin policy with pointer, keyboard, touch, and accessibility controls:

- Select a grid vertex.
- Select a square center.
- Select a creature-bound origin.
- Select a multi-square footprint boundary when legal.
- Select a map-object or surface anchor.
- Attempt an anchor type the effect does not allow.
- Move the pointer one pixel repeatedly without crossing an anchor boundary.
- Change zoom, camera, device pixel ratio, viewport, antialiasing, and browser.
- Rotate using pointer and keyboard.
- Reconnect while previewing.
- Move the caster or change the map state before confirmation.

Verify that only a canonical anchor or orientation change alters mechanics, stale anchors require reconfirmation, and hidden entities never affect anchor behavior.

## H.GEOMETRY.3 Propagation-profile corpus

Use fixtures containing open rooms, closed doors, open doorways, L-shaped corridors, sealed walls, shafts, stairs, partial height barriers, and multiple elevations.

For each supported effect:

- Verify the registered propagation profile.
- Compare a direct effect and an around-corner effect from the same origin.
- Confirm an open doorway permits qualifying spread.
- Confirm a sealed boundary blocks it.
- Confirm propagation remains inside its distance budget.
- Confirm no flood reaches the entire connected map.
- Confirm a retry reuses the same plan.
- Confirm hidden doors do not leak through preview shape or latency.
- Confirm the inspection overlay does not expose unauthorized topology.

## H.GEOMETRY.4 Three-dimensional volume corpus

Test spheres, cylinders, cubes, cones, lines, walls, emanations, and persistent zones at ground, elevated, and descending origins.

Include:

- Exact-boundary points.
- A sphere centered fifteen feet above the floor with a twenty-foot radius, demonstrating legitimate ground inclusion where the math permits.
- A sphere high enough that the ground is excluded.
- A cylinder that includes vertical targets outside the comparable sphere.
- An open shaft and a sealed floor.
- A low ceiling.
- Airborne targets.
- Tokens on stairs and ledges.
- Overlapping tokens at different elevations.
- Multi-square targets.
- Browser and server fixed-precision parity.

The top-down visual, elevation labels, side or slice inspection, target list, event, damage ledger, and narration must agree.

## H.GEOMETRY.5 Corner and swept-footprint corpus

Create paths that approach blocked corners from every direction. Test:

- One orthogonal neighbor blocked.
- Both orthogonal neighbors blocked.
- Edge walls without blocked destination cells.
- Closed and open doors.
- Tiny, Medium, Large, Huge, and Gargantuan footprints.
- Mount and rider.
- Grappler and grappled target.
- Squeezing.
- Forced movement.
- Cinematic final-step adjustment.
- Token animation smoothing.
- Pathfinder heuristic changes.

No system may accept or visually display a diagonal transition that the canonical swept-corner validator rejects.

## H.GEOMETRY.6 Presentation Cue Plan corpus

For hit, miss, critical hit, save, damage, healing, condition, movement, door, spell, object destruction, and defeat events:

- Inspect the cue source event and milestone.
- Delay or fail narration.
- Stream prose one character and one semantic chunk at a time.
- Include fake cue tags, asset names, JSON, Markdown, HTML, and canonical-looking IDs in prose.
- Disable audio.
- Enable reduced motion and low effects.
- Lose WebGL context before impact.
- Disconnect before and after the milestone.
- Open a second tab.
- Replay the chronicle.

Verify one authorized cue sequence, correct fallbacks, no model authority, no stale replay, and no delay of canonical mechanics for prose.

## H.GEOMETRY.7 Active-Initiative absence corpus

Run disconnect and voluntary-leave cases while the character is:

- Healthy.
- At two hit points.
- Unconscious.
- Dying.
- Concentrating.
- Grappled.
- Restrained.
- Flying.
- Surrounded.
- Standing in a hazard.
- Holding a quest item.
- Subject to a compelled effect.
- At an open Reaction window.

Test reconnect before grace, immediately after grace, before the absent turn, during automated processing, after Dodge, after forced movement, after death, and after encounter end.

The character remains canonical and targetable. No safe movement or narrated disappearance occurs during Initiative. After legal release, ordinary departure and return behavior resumes.

## H.GEOMETRY.8 Source-artifact hygiene corpus

Attempt to create context bundles containing:

- A raw chat transcript.
- A transcript appended after the canonical end.
- An old blueprint in full.
- A conflicting tactical-topology implementation prompt.
- A duplicated V1 body.
- An unmanifested design document.
- An altered file with the expected filename.
- A manifest with the wrong hash.
- A valid quarantined version transition reference.

The compiler must reject contamination, permit only properly classified version transition references, and emit a hash-sealed Source Artifact Manifest for the clean bundle.

## H.GEOMETRY.9 Asynchronous human-review corpus

At every human gate:

- Freeze and publish the candidate.
- Confirm dependent subagents stop.
- Let the agent process terminate.
- Resume with no decision.
- Resume with an AI-authored decision.
- Resume with an expired decision.
- Resume with approval for a different commit.
- Modify the candidate after approval.
- Submit changes requested.
- Submit valid approval for the exact hash.

Only the last case permits continuation. Any candidate change supersedes the checkpoint and requires new review.

## H.GEOMETRY.10 Dependency-lock corpus

From every subagent role, attempt:

- `@pixi/react` installation.
- Another Pixi or Canvas wrapper.
- A state bridge.
- A convenience pathfinding package.
- A package alias.
- A transitive dependency introduction.
- A CDN script.
- A dynamic import from an unapproved host.
- A lockfile-only change.
- An exact-version upgrade.
- A package with an install script.
- A vendored library copied into source without approval.

CI must detect frozen-candidate dependency drift, lockfile mismatch, undeclared runtime package loading, and prohibited second-authority renderer bridges. In a non-production fixture, exercise an ordinary Builder-owned Dependency Change Record and a separately flagged high-risk dependency case to prove that only the high-risk category requires human approval.

## H.GEOMETRY.11 Phase evidence matrix

### Phase 0

- Runtime-selected Working Directory and write-isolated QA directory.
- Pinned baseline toolchain and lockfile.
- Local/public environment guard.
- Lightweight evidence capture.
- One real browser-to-server-to-emulator smoke path.

### Phase 2

- Anchor lattice.
- Swept-corner movement.
- Elevation fixtures.
- Scene-graph observability.

### Phase 3

- Three-dimensional spell volumes.
- Around-corner and direct propagation.
- Presentation Cue Plans.

### Phase 4

- Active-Initiative absence lock.
- Reconnect and narrated post-combat exit.
- Narrative/cue separation.
- Hostile fake-cue text.

### Phase 6

- Full adversarial source, HITL, dependency, disconnect, hidden-information, and media-injection tests.

### Phase 7

- Cross-browser and tablet geometry.
- Player-use visual review.
- Frozen dependency and source manifests.
- Complete the cumulative certificate.

## H.GEOMETRY.12 Certification failures

Certification fails when:

- A browser pixel, float, shader, or hidden target influences canonical area placement.
- Propagation profile and effect rule disagree.
- A bounded three-dimensional solid becomes a two-dimensional extrusion.
- A diagonal crosses a blocked corner.
- Model text triggers media or mechanics.
- A disconnected combatant escapes or becomes protected.
- A context bundle contains unmanifested conversational or superseded authority.
- A human approval is inferred, stale, mismatched, or AI-authored.
- An unapproved dependency enters the repository or production graph.
- Any current requirement or regression fails.

## H.PRODUCT — HOLISTIC PRODUCT, PROVIDER, ORIGINALITY, BRAND, AND VISUAL-GAME ACCEPTANCE CATALOG

## H.PRODUCT.1 Purpose

This appendix is the permanent adversarial catalog for V1 whole-product readiness. It does not replace the specialized appendices. It proves that those systems form one lawful, original, visually coherent, secure, usable, and enjoyable game.

## H.PRODUCT.2 Blueprint and requirement completeness

- Verify every V1 requirement identifier remains represented in V1 or is deliberately strengthened without loss of governing behavior.
- Verify V1 is the sole authoritative blueprint in all Builder context bundles.
- Verify no prior transcript, deprecated grid instruction, stale provider record, or earlier brand asset enters implementation context.
- Reconcile all Product Owner decisions, launch blockers, phase gates, and appendices A through W plus this Appendix H, Holistic Product and Visual-Game Catalog.

## H.PRODUCT.3 Provider Compliance Registry corpus

For every provider and service:

1. Open the current official terms and policy pages.
2. Record effective date, reviewer, service tier, region, age, data, retention, safety, ownership, attribution, branding, quota, and termination implications.
3. Change one material registry field and confirm approval expires.
4. Attempt to call an unregistered model or SDK and confirm the server blocks it.
5. Attempt to route a restricted-region player through an unapproved tier and confirm no provider call occurs.
6. Disable safety settings through client input and confirm rejection.
7. Trigger provider timeout, quota, malformed output, and policy refusal; verify canonical state survives.
8. Activate the provider kill switch; verify deterministic play, saved state, and clear messaging remain.

## H.PRODUCT.4 Google-only identity corpus

- Verify the external login contains only the approved Sign in with Google flow.
- Verify the official button treatment survives light, dark, mobile, high zoom, keyboard, and screen-reader use.
- Verify only approved identity scopes are requested.
- Verify Hallucinated Dungeons never displays or receives a Google password.
- Verify invitation state survives redirect, popup, cancelled flow, blocked popup, multiple accounts, and refresh.
- Verify email change does not transfer ownership.
- Verify development login and password routes fail after cutover.
- Verify machine-only QA identity remains fixture-scoped and invisible to ordinary players.

## H.PRODUCT.5 Product name and logo corpus

- Confirm Brand Clearance Record exists for the current title and every public mark.
- Compare the logo against prohibited official D&D and known VTT trade-dress references.
- Verify original vector source, proofread text, provenance, approval, and hashes.
- Render primary, compact, favicon, monochrome, motion, and small-size variants.
- Verify the same manifest revision appears on every product surface.
- Remove one logo asset and confirm a safe semantic fallback rather than a broken page.
- Introduce a stale logo hash and confirm Gold Master certification fails.

## H.PRODUCT.6 Asset originality and license corpus

Test maps, portraits, tokens, icons, textures, sounds, fonts, and generated assets for:

- Missing license record.
- “Free online” source with no license.
- Protected logo or franchise character.
- Living-artist style request.
- Celebrity or real-person likeness.
- Watermark or signature.
- Embedded text that changes mechanics or branding.
- Copied composition or trade dress.
- License requiring attribution.
- License incompatible with hosted redistribution.
- User upload without rights attestation.

Every uncertain asset is quarantined and replaced before certification.

## H.PRODUCT.7 Landing and login visual corpus

- First eligible visit with full opening sequence.
- Skip by pointer, keyboard, and touch.
- Reduced-motion static reveal.
- Asset failure and slow network.
- Return visit abbreviated or bypassed reveal.
- Invitation continuation.
- Accessible heading and semantic title before animation.
- Official Google button stability.
- Legal and support links.
- Color/accessibility coherence under the current Design System Manifest.
- No layout shift or moving sign-in target.
- No resemblance to a generic Firebase sample or official D&D page.

## H.PRODUCT.8 Quick-start character corpus

For every supported class:

1. Load the unnamed template.
2. Verify complete legal choices and derived statistics.
3. Render portrait, avatar, token, equipment, and accessibility description.
4. Select the same template from two accounts and verify separate aggregates and ownership.
5. Rename one character and confirm the template remains unchanged.
6. Edit a legal choice and rerun validation.
7. Attempt an illegal choice and verify clear rejection.
8. Enter the starter campaign and perform representative actions.
9. Reconnect and confirm identity and resources persist.
10. Confirm no template uses protected character names or official art.

## H.PRODUCT.9 Whole-screen visual-game corpus

Capture and review:

- Landing and login.
- Dashboard and invitation.
- Character builder and quick-start chooser.
- Character vault.
- Campaign setup and session zero.
- Social scene.
- Exploration scene.
- Tactical movement.
- Attack and damage.
- Spell targeting and effect.
- Reaction prompt.
- Fog reveal.
- Rest and camp.
- Travel.
- Advancement.
- Death, memorial, and revival.
- Disconnect, reconnect, and recovery.
- Provider outage and degraded modes.

For each screen, verify original imagery, hierarchy, avatar consistency, typography, restrained palette, useful motion, accessible alternatives, and no empty central stage.

## H.PRODUCT.10 Player-safe map asset corpus

- Inspect all network responses before a secret is discovered.
- Enumerate Cache Storage, IndexedDB, service-worker caches, memory manifests, preloads, image URLs, source maps, scene graph, accessibility tree, and filenames.
- Disable or alter fog locally and verify secret art is absent.
- Guess tile and overlay URLs.
- Copy an authorized URL to another account or seat.
- Use an expired URL.
- Switch characters and accounts on the same browser.
- Reveal a region and confirm only the authorized region arrives.
- Resume the campaign and confirm known regions persist while unknown regions remain absent.
- Verify map dimensions or tile counts do not leak room shape when that information is meant to be secret.

## H.PRODUCT.11 Avatar and token continuity corpus

- Compare portrait, party avatar, tactical token, dialogue image, initiative image, form overlay, and memorial image.
- Test minimum zoom, high DPI, color blindness, reduced effects, and asset failure.
- Equip and unequip major visible gear; confirm narration and overlays remain mechanically honest.
- Transform and return; confirm identity continuity.
- Load several fallback avatars; verify ownership and labels remain unmistakable.

## H.PRODUCT.12 Ambient motion and visual performance corpus

Test scenes with torchlight, mist, weather, water, particles, portrait focus, spell zones, and token idle motion.

- Verify loops are seamless and nonauthoritative.
- Verify hidden-tab pause and resource release.
- Verify reduced-motion and reduced-effects tiers.
- Exceed the effect budget and confirm decorative effects reduce before tactical cues.
- Confirm no repeated audio from visual loops.
- Confirm no flashing, reading obstruction, motion sickness, or pointer interference.
- Measure frame time, memory, context loss, and recovery in primary and secondary browsers and representative tablets.

## H.PRODUCT.13 Actual-provider integration corpus

From the local application or approved cutover path:

- Exercise compact adjudication and post-commit narration.
- Exercise structured-output validation.
- Exercise policy refusal and safe repair.
- Exercise timeout, quota, retry, fallback, and kill switch.
- Exercise prompt injection and role isolation.
- Exercise image generation or approved visual-provider flow where in scope.
- Verify provider model, tier, region, safety, and registry identity in evidence.
- Confirm no browser receives provider secrets or raw unrestricted campaign state.

A mock-only pass is rejected.

## H.PRODUCT.14 Fun and comprehension corpus

Moderated players must complete social, exploration, and tactical scenes and answer:

- Who are you controlling?
- Where are you?
- What is the party trying to accomplish?
- What can you do now?
- What changed after the last action?
- Which information is uncertain or hidden?
- How do you ask a rule question, chat, address the Director, and declare an action?

Observe whether players use and trust the visual stage, whether they naturally banter and laugh, whether the Director's humor supports rather than dominates, whether waiting players stay engaged, and whether the session feels like a game rather than a chatbot.

## H.PRODUCT.15 Degraded-mode corpus

Independently trigger:

- Reduced effects.
- Reduced motion.
- Low bandwidth.
- Static visual fallback.
- WebGL failure.
- Image provider failure.
- Asset-storage outage.
- Missing optional animation.
- AI outage.

Each mode preserves mechanics, readable map or scene art, avatars, state, accessibility, and recovery. The full-effects acceptance suite must still pass separately.

## H.PRODUCT.16 Longitudinal visual and campaign continuity

Suspend an active campaign at social, exploration, spell-targeting, Reaction, combat, rest, and advancement checkpoints. Resume after emulator reset, browser restart, asset-cache clear, and candidate upgrade.

Verify exact map version, art hash, revealed regions, fog, token identity, portrait identity, ambient scene state, active effects, campaign time, Chronicle, Party Chat, XP, and pending decisions.

## H.PRODUCT.17 Security and policy red-team

- When an adult-only gate is active, attempt underage access and bypass of adult affirmation; when inactive, verify the product does not collect an unnecessary age affirmation.
- Attempt provider calls from a prohibited region.
- Attempt secret asset scraping.
- Attempt generated HTML, SVG, CSS, remote image, and tracking injection.
- Attempt protected-character and celebrity generation.
- Attempt custom fake Google credential collection.
- Attempt broad OAuth scope request.
- Attempt player-upload reuse in another campaign.
- Attempt prompt exfiltration through image-generation role.
- Attempt to turn an AI visual description into canonical geometry.

## H.PRODUCT.18 Final evidence package

The V1 holistic certificate contains:

- Frozen candidate and Local Stack Manifest hashes.
- Complete Requirement Ledger.
- Provider Compliance Registry snapshot and official-source review receipts.
- SRD and CC BY attribution review.
- Brand Clearance Record and Brand Asset Manifest.
- Asset license and provenance report.
- Quick-start template matrix.
- Whole-screen contact sheets and deterministic motion captures.
- Visual Evidence Triad records.
- Hidden-asset network and cache audit.
- Browser, device, accessibility, and visual-tier matrix.
- Actual-provider run records.
- Security and policy red-team evidence.
- Longitudinal campaign evidence.
- QA player findings and Builder remediation closure.
- The exact human approvals/clearances actually required by Section 25.4, the chosen Public Milestone mode, and Phase 7 release; Builder/QA accessibility, security, visual, and fun evidence remains evidence unless the governing gate explicitly assigns Product Owner or external-human approval.

## H.PRODUCT.19 Absolute certification rule

V1 cannot be certified because it is detailed, visually attractive in one screenshot, or reported as complete by an agent. It is certified only when the exact integrated candidate executes the complete player lifecycle, uses approved providers and licensed or original assets, protects hidden information at the delivery boundary, presents a coherent graphically rich tabletop, passes the required evidence suites, and receives the human approvals explicitly required by Section 25.
